explanations.explanation: White occupies the center and controls d5. The pawn move also opens diagonals for the queen and king’s bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5

explanations.explanation: Black matches White’s central presence and controls d4. The e5 pawn is undefended for now, so White can develop while attacking it.

explanations.explanation: White develops a knight, attacks the e5 pawn, and supports d4. Moving the knight also clears a square needed for kingside castling.

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7, a pawn defended only by the king. White is ready to castle and may later build a pawn center with c3 and d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5

explanations.explanation: White’s bishop pressures the knight that defends e5. Capturing the knight does not immediately win the pawn, but the pressure can support White’s central plans.

explanation.moves: e4 c5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black uses the c-pawn to control d4 without mirroring White’s central pawn. A later exchange on d4 can leave Black with an extra central pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6
explanation.title: French Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...d5 with pawn support, challenging White’s center. The trade-off is that the e6 pawn restricts Black’s light-squared bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...d5 with support from the c-pawn. Unlike ...e6, this leaves a diagonal open for the c8 bishop, but the c6 pawn occupies the knight’s usual square.

explanation.moves: e4 d5

explanations.explanation: Black immediately attacks the e4 pawn. After the common exd5, an early queen recapture can let White develop a piece while attacking the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn controls e5, preparing ...Nf6. Black often follows with ...g6 and ...Bg7, aiming at the center from a distance.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops a knight and immediately attacks e4. White can gain space with e5, but Black hopes to challenge an advanced pawn center later.

explanation.moves: d4 d5

explanations.explanation: Black claims central space and controls e4, making it harder for White to establish pawns on both d4 and e4. White can challenge the d5 pawn with c4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6

explanation.moves: Nf3 e5
explanation.title: Réti Opening: Ross Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the e-pawn, which White’s f3 knight can capture. Black hopes to gain activity in return for the pawn.

explanation.moves: Nf3 f5
explanation.title: Réti Opening: 1...f5

explanations.explanation: Black controls e4 with the f-pawn. If White later plays d4, the position may transpose into a Dutch Defense.

explanation.moves: b3 Nf6
explanation.title: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: 1...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and controls e4 without committing a central pawn. White can continue with Bb2.

explanation.moves: b3 c5
explanation.title: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: 1...c5

explanations.explanation: Black controls d4 from the flank. White can develop the c1 bishop to b2 and decide later how to arrange the center.

explanation.moves: b3 d5
explanation.title: Nimzo-Larsen Attack: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies the center and controls e4. White can continue with Bb2, aiming along the long diagonal.

explanation.moves: Nc3 Nc6
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queenside knight without committing a central pawn. White can choose how to build the center.

explanation.moves: Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and controls e4. Both sides keep several central pawn moves available.

explanation.moves: Nc3 c5
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...c5

explanations.explanation: Black controls d4 with the c-pawn. White can play e4 to reach a Sicilian position or choose a different setup.

explanation.moves: Nc3 c6
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...c6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares a possible ...d5 supported by the c-pawn. White’s next central move can steer the game into different openings.

explanation.moves: Nc3 d5
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies the center with the d-pawn. A later ...d4 could gain space and attack White’s c3 knight.

explanation.moves: g3 Nf6
explanation.title: King’s Fianchetto Opening: 1...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and controls e4. White can continue with Bg2 while both sides keep flexible pawn structures.

explanation.moves: g3 d5
explanation.title: King’s Fianchetto Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies the center and controls e4. White can develop the bishop to g2 and challenge the center from a distance.

explanation.moves: g3 g6
explanation.title: King’s Fianchetto Opening: 1...g6

explanations.explanation: Black mirrors White’s setup and prepares to develop the bishop to g7. Both sides can influence the center along the long diagonals.

explanation.moves: g3 b6
explanation.title: King’s Fianchetto Opening: 1...b6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop to b7, aiming along the same long diagonal White’s bishop may use from g2.

explanation.moves: f4 c5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 1...c5

explanations.explanation: Black controls d4 with the c-pawn. White may continue developing or play e4 to reach a Sicilian position.

explanation.moves: f4 d5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies the center and controls e4. The position resembles a Dutch Defense with colors reversed.

explanation.moves: f4 e6
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 1...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the queen. White’s early f-pawn advance leaves the diagonal toward the king more exposed.

explanation.moves: f4 f5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 1...f5

explanations.explanation: Black mirrors White and controls e4. Both sides have advanced their f-pawns and must consider the resulting kingside weaknesses.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to c5, where it pressures f2. The knight still defends e5, but remains under pressure.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: Center Fork

explanations.explanation: White takes e5, offering the knight. If Black captures it with the c6 knight, White can consider a central pawn fork with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 O-O
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: 4. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, bringing the rook to f1 and strengthening the king’s position. The rook changes the tactics after a possible exchange on c6 and capture on e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: Central Variation

explanations.explanation: The c-pawn supports d4, which would build a center and attack the bishop. The pawn also gives the queen access to a4 in some lines.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 Nf6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks e4. White can challenge the bishop with d4, though exchanges can lead to tactical counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 d5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: Konikowski Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black challenges e4 and opens the queen’s line. The bishop pins the c6 knight to the king, leaving Black’s center exposed to tactics.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bc5 c3 f5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defense: Cordel Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 with the f-pawn, offering a sharp central exchange. The c3 pawn means White cannot defend e4 with Nc3 here.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Na5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Pollock Defense

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight again, leaving e5 without its knight defender. White can consider Nxe5, but should still examine Black’s tactical replies.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nb8
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Retreat Variation

explanations.explanation: Black returns the knight to b8, giving up its development and leaving e5 without that defender.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nce7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: 3...Nce7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight to e7, blocking the bishop and leaving e5 undefended. White can capture the pawn with Nxe5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense

explanations.explanation: Black abandons the defense of e5 and attacks the bishop. After an exchange on d4, Black may recapture with the e-pawn and gain central space.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Bc4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense: 4. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White moves the bishop away from attack and targets f7. Black can consider exchanging on f3 or developing the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense: 4. Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight on d4. Black can recapture with ...exd4, gaining an advanced central pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense: 4...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures and gains a pawn on d4. Black can support it with the bishop or prepare ...c6 and ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops a knight and attacks e4. White can defend the pawn or castle, allowing Black to take it while relying on counterplay against e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense: 4. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the rook on f1 while leaving e4 under attack. If Black takes it, White can use the e-file and pressure e5 to regain the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Bc5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense: Beverwijk Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to c5, where it pressures f2. White can consider Nxe5, exploiting tactics involving the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Ng4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Berlin Defense: Fishing Pole

explanations.explanation: Black places the knight on g4. The move can set a trap involving ...h5 after h3, so White should consider the consequences before attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Berlin

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e4 pawn. White can challenge the knight and recover e5, for example by bringing the rook to e1.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Berlin: 5. d4

explanations.explanation: White attacks e5 and opens lines while a pawn down. The rook may come to e1, adding pressure along the e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Anti-Berlin

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and keeps a quieter structure than after castling and allowing ...Nxe4. The support for e4 also affects tactics around e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Bc5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Anti-Berlin: 4...Bc5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, controlling d4 and preparing to castle. White can support a later d4 with c3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Ne7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Anti-Berlin: Mortimer Variation

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight, blocking the bishop but setting a trap. Capturing e5 immediately can allow ...c6 followed by a queen check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nge7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Cozio Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to e7, leaving the f-pawn free but blocking the bishop. Black may later move the knight again or fianchetto the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Qe7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Vinogradov Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen supports e5, but also occupies the bishop’s diagonal. A future rook on e1 could face the queen along the e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Qf6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Frankfurt Defense

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen supports the c6 knight and defends e5. Early queen development also occupies the usual knight square.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White exchanges the bishop for the knight, removing a defender of e5. Black can recapture, accepting a changed pawn structure in return for the bishop pair.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation: 4...dxc6

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures with the d-pawn, opening lines for the c8 bishop and queen. The doubled c-pawns are a lasting structural feature.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 Nxe5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation: 5. Nxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures e5, but Black can play ...Qd4, attacking the knight and threatening f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation: 5. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the rook on f1. This changes the consequences of ...Qd4 after a later capture on e5, since the rook protects f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defense: 5. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles and can defend e4 with Re1. Black can develop, castle, or capture the pawn and enter the Open Spanish.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Caro Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop, breaking its pressure on the knight. White can retreat to b3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bb3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Caro Variation: 5. Bb3

explanations.explanation: White preserves the bishop on b3, where it pressures f7. Black has gained queenside space with ...b5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Spanish Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black immediately attacks e4, offering a central pawn while the bishop attacks the knight. The center can open quickly.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Steinitz Defense

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5 with the d-pawn. This gives the center additional support but restricts the f8 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Schliemann Defense

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 with the f-pawn, creating an immediate central confrontation. White can defend e4 with Nc3 or choose another response.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Nürnberg Variation

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5 with the f-pawn. The pawn also occupies the kingside knight’s usual square and weakens the area around the king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 g5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Brentano Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black advances the g-pawn, preparing to challenge the knight. White can strike in the center with d4, opening the bishop’s diagonal toward g5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 g6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Fianchetto Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop to g7, aiming along the long diagonal. White can continue developing or castle.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Bc5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Møller Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to c5 before advancing the b-pawn. White can prepare a center with c3 or exchange on c6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Closed Spanish

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to e7 and prepares castling. The bishop shields the king from tactics along the e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Bxc6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Delayed Exchange

explanations.explanation: White exchanges the bishop for the knight after Black has committed the other knight to f6. This removes a defender of e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Qe2
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Worrall Attack

explanations.explanation: The queen defends e4, leaving the rook free to move to d1 in support of a later d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Closed Spanish: 6. Re1

explanations.explanation: The rook supports e4. White renews pressure on e5 by threatening to exchange the knight that defends it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Closed Spanish: 6...b5

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop and interrupts its pressure on the c6 knight. White can retreat to b3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Spanish

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e4 pawn. White can challenge the center with d4 and exploit the alignment of Black’s knight and king on the e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 Re1
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Spanish: 6. Re1

explanations.explanation: White brings the rook to the open e-file, attacking the knight. Black can respond with ...Nc5, attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Spanish: 6. d4

explanations.explanation: White attacks e5 and opens lines while Black’s king remains on e8. Black must address the pressure and continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 b5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Spanish: 6...b5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the bishop, cutting off its pressure on the knight. White usually preserves the bishop on b3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Open Spanish: Riga Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures on d4, temporarily taking a second pawn. The knight on e4 and uncastled king make the open e-file a source of tactics.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defense: 5...b5

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop. White can retreat to b3, keeping the bishop on the board.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Morphy Defense: 6. Bb3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop, which now pressures f7. Black can choose among several bishop developments and central setups.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3 Bb7
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Arkhangelsk Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to b7, aiming along the long diagonal toward White’s center. The bishop also defends the rook.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O b5 Bb3 Bc5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Modern Arkhangelsk Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to c5, where it pressures f2. The other bishop retains more than one possible development square.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White challenges the c5 pawn with d4. After ...cxd4, White can recapture with the knight, opening lines while Black retains two central pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Nc3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and keeps several plans open, including a later d4 break or a more closed setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 c3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Delayed Alapin

explanations.explanation: White plays c3 to support a later d4, aiming for a strong pawn center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Rossolimo Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and pressures the c6 knight. White can castle and choose between a quiet d3 setup and a later d4 break.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Nc3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight while postponing the decision to open the center with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White challenges the c5 pawn and threatens to advance to d5, displacing the knight. After ...cxd4, White can recapture with the f3 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3
explanation.title: Italian Game: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: The c3 pawn supports d4, preparing a broader pawn center. Black can develop with ...Nf6 and attack the e4 pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3
explanation.title: Italian Game: Giuoco Pianissimo

explanations.explanation: White supports the e4 pawn and postpones d4, choosing a slower buildup. A later c3 can help prepare the central advance.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn to divert Black’s bishop. If Black captures it, c3 can attack the bishop while preparing d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O
explanation.title: Italian Game: 4. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, bringing the king to safety and the rook to f1. A later d3 can lead to a quieter Italian setup.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, adding pressure on d5 and supporting a possible later e4 advance.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nf3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, bringing kingside castling closer while keeping options for the other knight.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 g3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 3. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares to develop the bishop to g2, combining a kingside fianchetto with the d4 and c4 pawns in a Catalan-style setup.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3
explanation.title: French Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend e4 and also adds pressure on d5. Black can develop with ...Nf6 or pin the knight with ...Bb4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2
explanation.title: French Defense: Tarrasch Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend e4, keeping c3 available for a pawn. The knight temporarily blocks the c1 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and prepares to recapture on e4 if Black exchanges pawns there.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 3. Nd2

explanations.explanation: White prepares to recapture on e4 with the knight while keeping c3 free for a pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White exchanges the e-pawn on d5. Black commonly recaptures with ...cxd5, after which White can develop or challenge the center with c4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: The f3 pawn supports e4. If Black captures there, White can recapture with the f-pawn and retain two central pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the c-pawn for White’s d-pawn, opening the c-file for Black. White can recapture with Nxd4, centralizing the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 4. Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures and centralizes the knight, which eyes b5. Black retains both central pawns and often develops with ...Nf6, attacking e4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the c-pawn for White’s d-pawn and keeps both central pawns. White can recapture with Nxd4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 4. Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight and opens lines for development. The d4 knight attacks the c6 knight, though exchanging it would allow Black to recapture with the b-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White challenges the c5 pawn, inviting an exchange. After ...cxd4 and Nxd4, White gains open lines while Black keeps two central pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 3...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the c-pawn for White’s d-pawn, reducing White’s central pawn presence. White can recapture with Nxd4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 4. Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight. Black can choose among several setups, including ...Nc6, ...a6, or ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4
explanation.title: French Defense: Winawer Variation

explanations.explanation: Black pins the c3 knight to the king, undermining its defense of e4. White often advances the e-pawn to e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5
explanation.title: French Defense: Winawer: 4. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, gaining space and moving it out of danger. Black often answers ...c5 to challenge the base of White’s pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: French Defense: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White can preserve the tension with Bg5 or advance e5 to attack the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4
explanation.title: French Defense: Rubinstein Variation

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges on e4, releasing the central tension. White usually recaptures with Nxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4
explanation.title: French Defense: Rubinstein: 4. Nxe4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight. Black can develop with ...Nf6 or prepare it with ...Nd7.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6
explanation.title: French Defense: Closed Tarrasch

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and adds pressure on e4. White often advances e5, gaining space and attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 3...dxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn, giving up the d-pawn to remove White’s two-pawn center. White usually recaptures with Nxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 4. Nxe4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight. Black has several developing choices, including ...Bf5, ...Nd7, and ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks the e4 knight. White often plays Ng3, attacking the bishop in turn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Exchange: 3...cxd5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures with the c-pawn. White can develop the bishop to d3 or challenge the center with c4, the Panov attack.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, defends d5, and moves closer to castling. White can develop the c1 bishop or exchange on d5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 4. Bg5

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and pins the f6 knight to Black’s queen.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Orthodox Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, breaking the pin on the f6 knight and preparing to castle.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Tarrasch Defense

explanations.explanation: Black challenges White’s center with the c-pawn. Exchanges can leave Black with an isolated d-pawn and active piece play.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Triangle System

explanations.explanation: Black reinforces the d5 pawn and keeps several setups available, including a later ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6
explanation.title: Italian Game: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White can defend with d3 or continue the central contest with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Italian Game: Giuoco Pianissimo

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and opens the c1 bishop’s diagonal. White can continue with castling and gradual development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black accepts the offered pawn with the bishop. White often plays c3, attacking the bishop while preparing d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks the e4 pawn. White commonly defends it while developing with Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 5. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend e4. Black can now choose among several setups, including the Najdorf, Dragon, and Classical variations.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Najdorf Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn controls b5, discouraging a knight or bishop from landing there. It also prepares possible queenside expansion with ...b5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White often defends the pawn with Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 5. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend e4. Black can choose among central pawn setups, including ...d6, ...e6, and ...e5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Löwenthal Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn to attack the d4 knight. White can move the knight to b5, where it pressures d6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Accelerated Dragon

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop to g7, keeping the option of advancing the d-pawn two squares in one move. White can answer with c4 to control d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 c4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Maróczy Bind

explanations.explanation: White’s c4 pawn and e4 pawn both control d5, making Black’s ...d5 break harder to arrange.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Winawer: 4...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the d4 pawn, the base of White’s pawn chain. White often replies a3, questioning the bishop on b4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical: 5. Ng3

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight to attack the f5 bishop. Black usually retreats it to g6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Classical: 5...Bg6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop. White often plays h4, preparing to gain space and question the bishop again.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3
explanation.title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit: 5. c3

explanations.explanation: White attacks the bishop and prepares a later d4 advance. Black must decide where to place the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5
explanation.title: Italian Game: Evans Gambit: 5...Ba5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop while keeping it active. White can continue the gambit with d4 to claim the center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 5. e3

explanations.explanation: White plays e3, supporting d4 and opening a diagonal for the f1 bishop. The c1 bishop has already developed outside the pawn chain.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7
explanation.title: King’s Indian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop in a fianchetto, allowing White central space while preparing to challenge it later.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4
explanation.title: King’s Indian Defense: 4. e4

explanations.explanation: White claims central space with the e-pawn. Black often replies ...d6, controlling e5 and preparing a later central challenge.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defense

explanations.explanation: Black immediately challenges White’s center with the d5 pawn. White can exchange on d5 and then build a pawn center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defense: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White captures on d5. Black usually recaptures with the knight, after which White can play e4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: White’s queen defends the c3 knight, allowing a queen recapture if Black exchanges the bishop for it.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 e3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Rubinstein Variation

explanations.explanation: White plays e3 to open a diagonal for the f1 bishop, continuing development without immediately challenging Black’s bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Sämisch Variation

explanations.explanation: White attacks the b4 bishop, asking Black whether to exchange it for the c3 knight.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 f3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian Defense: Kmoch Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares to support an e4 advance with the f-pawn, aiming for a broad center at the cost of slower development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, adding pressure on d5 and supporting a possible e4 advance.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls e5. Black commonly develops with ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, adding protection to d5 and controlling e4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White captures on d5, releasing the central tension. Black usually recaptures with the c-pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Exchange: 3...cxd5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures with the c-pawn, producing a symmetrical pawn structure. Both sides can continue developing their pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bc4
explanation.title: Sicilian Najdorf: Fischer–Sozin Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop to pressure f7. Black often responds with ...e6, limiting the bishop’s diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be2
explanation.title: Sicilian Najdorf: Opocensky Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, preparing kingside castling while keeping a flexible setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Be3
explanation.title: Sicilian Najdorf: English Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, often preparing queenside castling and a pawn advance on the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5
explanation.title: Sicilian Najdorf: 6. Bg5

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and attacks the f6 knight. An exchange on f6 can leave Black with doubled f-pawns.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6
explanation.title: King’s Indian Defense: 4...d6

explanations.explanation: Black controls e5, making it harder for White to advance the e-pawn with tempo. Black keeps ...e5 and ...c5 as possible central breaks.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 O-O
explanation.title: King’s Indian Defense: 4...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles, moving the king to safety. Play can return to familiar King’s Indian setups after White develops and Black plays ...d6.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defense: 4...Nxd5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures with the knight. White can advance e4, gaining space and attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: 6. d4

explanations.explanation: White occupies the center and attacks the e5 pawn. Black can capture on d4 or reinforce the center.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 6. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, moving closer to kingside castling. Black often develops with ...Nd7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 6. h4

explanations.explanation: White advances the h-pawn, preparing h5 to attack the bishop on g6. Black commonly replies ...h6 to give the bishop a retreat.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the second knight, adding pressure on d5. Black can choose between the Semi-Slav, capturing on c4, and other setups.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Qc2
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 4. Qc2

explanations.explanation: The queen defends the c4 pawn and supports a possible e4 advance. Black can still capture on c4, when White may recapture with the queen.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 cxd5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White captures on d5, releasing the central tension. Black commonly recaptures with the c-pawn.

explanations.explanation: White plays e3, supporting d4 and opening a line for the f1 bishop while leaving the b1 knight’s development flexible.

explanations.explanation: Black plays e6, retaining a flexible central pawn structure and opening a diagonal for the f8 bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3
explanation.title: King’s Indian: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and supports e4. Black commonly castles before challenging White’s center.

explanations.explanation: White’s f-pawn reinforces e4. The move supports the center but occupies the knight’s usual developing square.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f4

explanations.explanation: White builds a broad center with the f-pawn alongside the c4, d4, and e4 pawns. Black will look for ways to challenge that center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4
explanation.title: Grünfeld: Exchange Variation: 5. e4

explanations.explanation: White claims central space and attacks the d5 knight. Black can exchange it for the c3 knight and later pressure White’s center.

explanations.explanation: White’s knight controls c5. White plans to gain central space with e4 and can consider bringing the knight to c5 later.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn defends e5. White can continue development or castle while maintaining the central tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 b5

explanations.explanation: Black offers the b-pawn, which White’s c4 bishop can capture. Black’s idea is to challenge the center with ...Nxd4 afterward.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6

explanations.explanation: Black moves the h-pawn, giving the bishop a retreat on h7 if White advances h5.

explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 6...h5

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 a6
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Chebanenko Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the a-pawn, preparing ...b5 to challenge White’s c-pawn or support a pawn captured on c4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn and may try to support it with ...b5. White can develop to recover the pawn or play a4 to hinder that advance.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop to g7. White can continue development or exchange pawns on d5.

explanations.explanation: White captures the undefended e-pawn. Black usually plays ...d6 to drive the knight away before recovering the pawn.

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn and attacks e5, aiming to open the center. Black can capture on e4 or d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d3

explanations.explanation: White defends the e4 pawn, allowing the knight on f3 to continue threatening e5.

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend e4. Black can develop ...Nc6, reaching a Four Knights position.

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop to pressure f7, but the e4 pawn remains attacked by Black’s knight.

explanations.explanation: White adds pressure on e5, challenging the pawn supported by Black’s d6 pawn. Black can exchange or add a defender.

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recapture with Nxd4 or offer the pawn for rapid development.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6
explanation.title: Sicilian Alapin: 2...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks the e4 pawn. White often advances e5, attacking the knight in turn.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 c3 d5
explanation.title: Sicilian Alapin: 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black immediately challenges the e4 pawn. White often captures on d5, when Black may recapture with the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qa5
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: 3...Qa5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the queen from the knight’s attack while keeping it active. White can gain central space with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd6
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: 3...Qd6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the queen while keeping it near the center. White can continue developing and may later attack the queen again.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 Nc3 Qd8
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: Valencian Variation

explanations.explanation: Black returns the queen to its starting square. White can take central space with d4 and continue developing.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls e5. Black often continues development with ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 3. e3

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 and opens a diagonal for the f1 bishop to recover the pawn on c4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 3. e4

explanations.explanation: White takes central space with the e-pawn and opens the f1 bishop’s diagonal toward the pawn on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Advance: 3...Bf5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before a possible ...e6. White can continue development or challenge the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Botvinnik–Carls Defense

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the d4 pawn, challenging the base of White’s pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Advance: 3...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4, the base of White’s pawn chain. White often supports it with c3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the e5 knight, preparing to recover the e4 pawn after the knight retreats.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to attack the e5 knight, offering a pawn for active play. If White exchanges knights, Black can recapture with the d-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Damiano Variation

explanations.explanation: Black immediately recaptures on e4. White can play Qe2, attacking the knight along the open e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight, centralizing it. Black can develop with ...Bc5 or ...Nf6 and attack White’s center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 Bc4
explanation.title: Scotch Gambit

explanations.explanation: White delays recapturing on d4 and develops the bishop to pressure f7, seeking rapid development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 exd4 c3
explanation.title: Scotch Game: Göring Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the c-pawn for faster development. If Black captures it, White can recapture with the b1 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 c3 Nf6 e5
explanation.title: Sicilian Alapin: 3. e5

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the f6 knight, which must move again. Black commonly retreats it to d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 c3 d5 exd5
explanation.title: Sicilian Alapin: 3. exd5

explanations.explanation: White captures on d5. Black often recaptures with the queen; the c3 pawn prevents an immediate Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3
explanation.title: French Defense: Advance: 4. c3

explanations.explanation: White supports d4, so the c-pawn can recapture if Black exchanges on d4. Black often adds pressure with ...Nc6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Advance: Short Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and prepares kingside castling. Black often continues ...e6 and later challenges the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls e4. White may also gain kingside space with g4 and h4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 g4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Advance: Bayonet Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the g-pawn to attack the bishop. The aggressive move gains time on the bishop but weakens White’s kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 h4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Advance: Tal Variation

explanations.explanation: White gains kingside space with the h-pawn and prepares g4 to challenge Black’s bishop. Black often answers ...h5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 e5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 3...e5

explanations.explanation: Black strikes back in the center and attacks d4. White can develop Nf3 to defend d4 and attack e5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: Greco Variation

explanations.explanation: Black defends the c4 pawn. White can challenge the pawn chain with a4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: Hanham Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to defend e5, preserving the central tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nc6
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: 3...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to defend e5. White can develop Bb5, pinning that knight to the king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: Nimzowitsch Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4, counterattacking while White threatens e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures on d4, releasing central tension. White usually recaptures with the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nf3
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 4. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the knight from the d6 pawn’s attack. Black can now recover the e4 pawn with ...Nxe4.

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop on b7. White can play d4, continuing toward an open Sicilian.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges the center with the d-pawn. After exd5 and ...Qxd5, White can develop Nc3 while attacking the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bb5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Moscow Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop with check. One plan is to exchange the bishop before setting up pawns on c4 and e4 to control d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Hyperaccelerated Dragon

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to fianchetto the bishop on g7. By delaying ...Nc6, Black avoids the immediate Bb5 check associated with the Rossolimo.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 a3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Mengarini Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares b4, a delayed wing gambit intended to divert Black’s c-pawn from the center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 b3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Czerniak Attack

explanations.explanation: White prepares to fianchetto the bishop on b2 and may delay opening the center. Black has several standard Sicilian setups available.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 b4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Wing Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn to divert Black’s c-pawn from its control of d4. Black can accept with ...cxb4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 c4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Staunton-Cochrane Variation

explanations.explanation: White’s c-pawn controls d5 alongside the e-pawn, restricting ...d5. The c-pawn can no longer support a d4 advance from c3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 2. d4

explanations.explanation: White offers the d-pawn to open the center immediately. After ...cxd4, White can offer another pawn with c3 in the Smith-Morra Gambit.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 2...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures a central pawn with the c-pawn. White can offer the Smith-Morra Gambit with c3 or prepare to recapture with Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 Nf3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Morphy Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and prepares to recapture on d4. Black can allow a transposition to an open Sicilian or support the pawn with ...e5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 Qxd4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 3. Qxd4

explanations.explanation: White recovers the pawn with the queen, but Black can develop ...Nc6 while attacking it.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Smith-Morra Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers a pawn with c3 for rapid development and open files. If Black captures, the knight can recapture on c3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 e5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 2. e5

explanations.explanation: White gains space and controls f6, restricting Black’s kingside knight. The advance does not add pressure to d4, where Black can continue to contest the center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 f4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: McDonnell Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the f-pawn as part of a kingside attacking setup. Black can challenge the center immediately with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 f4 d5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Tal Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the d-pawn to disrupt White’s attacking setup. After exd5, Black can develop a knight and seek activity rather than recapturing immediately.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Bc4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Hillbilly Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop early. Black can play ...d5, challenging the center and attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Bc4 d5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Hillbilly, 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the bishop while challenging e4. White can exchange on d5 or retreat the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Bc4 d5 Bb3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Schaeffer Gambit

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop and leaves e4 exposed. Black can accept the pawn with ...dxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and supports e4, postponing d4. After ...d5 White can choose d4 or continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black follows through with ...d5, attacking e4. White can develop Nf3 or play d4 to enter a classical Caro-Kann position.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Bg4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Two Knights, 3...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the knight to the queen. White may question the bishop with h3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Nf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Two Knights, 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and adds pressure on e4. White can advance e5, attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 2. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls d4 without committing the d-pawn. After ...d5, several Caro-Kann lines remain available by transposition.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nf3 d5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: 2...d5 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black plays ...d5, attacking e4, supported by the c6 pawn. White can exchange or develop the other knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 b3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Euwe Attack

explanations.explanation: White prepares to develop the bishop on b2. Black can continue the usual central plan with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 c4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Accelerated Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White plays c4 early: the c-pawn and e-pawn both control d5. This differs from the Panov reached after an exchange on d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Breyer Variation

explanations.explanation: White supports e4 instead of immediately playing d4. The setup can lead to an early exchange or a King’s Indian Attack formation.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Breyer, 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 with support from c6. An exchange on e4 can open the d-file and create the possibility of a queen trade.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Breyer Endgame Offer

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls e5. After ...dxe4 and dxe4, Black can exchange queens on d1.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3 dxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Breyer, 3...dxe4

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges on e4. White can recapture with the d-pawn, after which ...Qxd1+ offers a queen exchange.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 Na6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: De Bruycker Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to a6 because the c6 pawn occupies its usual square. The knight may later move to c7 before Black plays ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 Na6 Bxa6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: De Bruycker, 3. Bxa6

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight. Black has the intermediate check ...Qa5+, intending to recover the bishop without doubling the a-pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defense: Mieses Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and prepares to recapture on e4. Black can exchange there, after which the bishop must move again to regain the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Mieses, 3...dxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn and releases central tension. White can recapture with Bxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 Qb6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Edinburgh Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks d4. White can support the pawn with c3 or develop a knight to f3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy, 3...dxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures on e4. White normally recaptures with fxe4, opening the f-file.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy, 3...e6

explanations.explanation: Black supports d5 and retains central tension. The position can transpose into French Defense structures after further development.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nc3
explanation.title: French Defense: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and supports e4. After ...d5, White can enter a French main line with d4 or continue with Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nc3 d5
explanation.title: French Defense: 2...d5 after Nc3

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4. White can support the center with d4 or develop Nf3; an exchange on d5 is another possibility.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3
explanation.title: French Defense: Knight Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the kingside knight before committing the d-pawn. Black can continue with ...d5 or choose a different structure.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5
explanation.title: French Defense: 2...d5 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 in the usual French fashion. White can defend the pawn with Nc3 or advance it to e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 Nc3
explanation.title: French Defense: Two Knights Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops both knights, with Nc3 supporting e4. Black can develop ...Nf6 or advance ...d4 to gain space and attack the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 e5
explanation.title: French Defense: 3. e5 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn to gain space and restrict Black’s development. Black often challenges the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 e5 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: 3...c5 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black plays ...c5, controlling d4. White can continue with d4, transposing into an Advance French, or offer the b-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Qe2
explanation.title: French Defense: Chigorin Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen to e2. If Black plays ...d5 and White captures on d5, the queen can pin the e6 pawn to the king, preventing an immediate pawn recapture.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Qe2 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Chigorin, 2...c5

explanations.explanation: Black controls d4, giving the game a Sicilian character. White can develop Nf3 and fianchetto the kingside bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 c4
explanation.title: French Defense: Steiner Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the c-pawn toward the center. After ...d5, exchanges can leave Black’s queen exposed to development with Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 c4 d5
explanation.title: French Defense: Steiner, 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges e4. White can exchange in the center or play the gambit move cxd5 before resolving the e-pawn tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d3
explanation.title: French Defense: King’s Indian Attack

explanations.explanation: White supports e4 and can develop in a King’s Indian Attack formation. A later e5 advance may gain space for a kingside attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d3 d5
explanation.title: French Defense: King’s Indian Attack, 2...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges e4. White can continue with Nd2 and a kingside fianchetto, or transpose into other openings.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d3 d5 Nd2
explanation.title: French Defense: King’s Indian Attack, 3. Nd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and prepares a King’s Indian Attack setup, often including Ngf3, g3 and Bg2. The knight adds support to e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 Nf6
explanation.title: French Defense: Mediterranean Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White can advance e5, gaining space with an attack on the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Franco-Benoni

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4. White can advance d5 for a Benoni-style position or develop Nf3, potentially transposing to a Sicilian.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Be3
explanation.title: French Defense: Alapin Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop while offering the e4 pawn. After ...dxe4, White can play f3 to challenge the advanced pawn and seek rapid development.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Marshall Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4 before White has advanced the e-pawn. White can exchange on d5 and then capture the offered c-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5
explanation.title: French Defense: Open Tarrasch

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4, which the knight on d2 has cut off from the queen. White often exchanges on d5, and Black must choose how to recapture.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5
explanation.title: French Defense: Exchange, 3...exd5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on d5, producing a symmetrical pawn structure. Both sides can develop pieces while choosing how to create imbalances.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 e5
explanation.title: French Defense: Steinitz Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn early, gaining space and controlling f6. Black can challenge the advanced pawn with ...d5 or ...d6.

explanation.moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: English Opening: 2. Nc3 against ...Nf6

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and reinforces control of d5. Black can choose a kingside fianchetto or an ...e6 setup.

explanation.moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 e6
explanation.title: English Opening: 2...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop and keeps several central setups available. A later ...Bb4 can pin the knight on c3.

explanation.moves: c4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
explanation.title: English Opening: 2...g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to fianchetto the bishop on g7. White can play d4 to enter a King’s Indian setup or continue in English fashion with g3.

explanation.moves: c4 c5 b4
explanation.title: English Opening: Queen’s Wing Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn to draw Black’s c-pawn away from its control of d4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4
explanation.title: Indian Defense: Accelerated London

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop before e3, keeping it outside the pawn chain. The bishop controls e5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6
explanation.title: London System: 2...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the bishop on f8 while postponing a central pawn advance. White can continue with e3.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3
explanation.title: London System: 3. e3

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 after developing the bishop outside the pawn chain. Black retains several ways to challenge the center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5
explanation.title: Indian Defense: Trompowsky Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and attacks the f6 knight. Black can move the knight, support it, or allow the exchange.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4
explanation.title: Trompowsky Attack: 2...Ne4

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight again and attacks the bishop. White commonly retreats the bishop to f4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 Bf4
explanation.title: Trompowsky Attack: 3. Bf4

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop from the knight’s attack while keeping it active. Both sides have moved a minor piece twice.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bg5 Ne4 h4
explanation.title: Trompowsky Attack: Raptor Variation

explanations.explanation: White defends the bishop with the h-pawn. If Black captures the bishop, hxg5 opens the h-file for White.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and supports e4. The knight occupies c3, preventing an immediate c4 advance.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 2...d5 after Nc3

explanations.explanation: Black controls e4 with both the d-pawn and knight. White can develop the bishop to f4 or g5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 Bf4
explanation.title: Jobava London System

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop alongside the c3 knight. A later Nb5 can create threats on c7, depending on Black’s response.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 Bg5
explanation.title: Richter-Veresov Attack

explanations.explanation: White pins the knight to the queen. An exchange on f6 can reduce Black’s control of the center and may leave doubled f-pawns.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 e4
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 3. e4 Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the e-pawn to open the center. After ...dxe4, the position enters a Blackmar-Diemer Gambit.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nd2 e5
explanation.title: Indian Defense: Lazard Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the e-pawn, inviting dxe5. The gambit seeks tactical chances, including a possible knight jump toward e3 in some lines.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 b5
explanation.title: Indian Defense: Polish Defense Deferred

explanations.explanation: Black advances the b-pawn, controlling c4, and prepares to fianchetto the queenside bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 c5
explanation.title: Spielmann-Indian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4 from the flank. White can advance d5, gaining central space in a Benoni-like structure.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 2...d5 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black claims central space and controls e4. White can play c4 to reach a Queen’s Gambit position or choose another system.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 d5 e3
explanation.title: Colle System

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 and plans an eventual e4 pawn break. The c1 bishop remains behind the pawn chain for now.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 e6
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 2...e6 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop, preparing development and kingside castling. The central structure remains flexible.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Nf3 g6
explanation.title: Indian Defense: 2...g6 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...Bg7 while keeping the d-pawn flexible. White has not yet committed the c-pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 Nc6
explanation.title: Black Knights’ Tango

explanations.explanation: Black develops both knights without committing a central pawn. The c6 knight pressures d4; White can develop Nf3 to control e5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 Nc6 Nc3
explanation.title: Black Knights’ Tango: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, pressuring d5 and supporting e4. Black may play ...e5 or prepare ...Bb4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 Nc6 Nf3
explanation.title: Black Knights’ Tango: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops and controls e5, making an immediate ...e5 harder. Black can support a central pawn advance.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bb5
explanation.title: Portuguese Opening

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop before Black has played ...Nc6. Black can gain time with ...c6, attacking it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, pressuring f7, while keeping the f-pawn free. The position can transpose into several open games.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Classical Defense

explanations.explanation: Black matches White’s development and aims at f2. White can consider d4, challenging the center and the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5 Qg4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 3. Qg4

explanations.explanation: White’s early queen attacks g7. Black must account for threats on the kingside while developing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5 Qh5
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Scholar’s Mate Threat

explanations.explanation: White’s queen and bishop both aim at f7, threatening mate. Black can defend the pawn while continuing development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5 Qh5 Qe7
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 3...Qe7

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen defends f7 against the immediate mating threat. The f6 square remains available for the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Be7
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...Be7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop but leaves e5 undefended. White can play Qh5, simultaneously attacking e5 and threatening f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nc6
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and defends e5. A later ...Na5 can attack the bishop on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Berlin Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. The knight also controls h5, discouraging Qh5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 3. d3

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and opens a diagonal for the c1 bishop. Black can choose ...c6 and ...d5 rather than immediately developing the queenside knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Ponziani-Urusov Gambit

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5 while the e4 pawn is attacked. Black can accept with ...exd4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Urusov Gambit: 3...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black accepts the offered d-pawn. White can develop while preparing to challenge or recover it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f3
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Walkerling Variation

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 with the f-pawn. This occupies the knight’s usual f3 square and weakens the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f3 d5
explanation.title: Walkerling Variation: 3...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges e4 and opens lines in the center. White can exchange with exd5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f3 d5 exd5
explanation.title: Walkerling Variation: 4. exd5

explanations.explanation: White exchanges on d5. Black can recapture with the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Greco Gambit

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5 but leaves e4 under attack. Black can take either pawn, with different gambit positions.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f4 Nxe4
explanation.title: Greco Gambit: 3...Nxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn with the knight. White can attack the knight with d3; an immediate fxe5 allows a dangerous ...Qh4+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 f4 Nxe4 d3
explanation.title: Greco Gambit: 4. d3

explanations.explanation: White’s d-pawn attacks the knight. Black must decide where to move it or look for active counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Qg5
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...Qg5

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks g2, but has moved out early. White can develop Nf3 while attacking the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Qh4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...Qh4

explanations.explanation: Black’s early queen attacks e4 and threatens check if it captures. White can develop Nc3 to defend the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 b5
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Anderssen Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop and is itself offered for capture. White can accept with Bxb5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 c6
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: Philidor Counterattack

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...d5, challenging White’s center with support from the c-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 d6
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...d6

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5 with a pawn. The move also restricts the f8 bishop, and Nf3 can transpose into a Philidor.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 g6
explanation.title: Bishop’s Opening: 2...g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...Bg7. White can seize central space with d4, attacking e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Ke2
explanation.title: Bongcloud Opening

explanations.explanation: White moves the king to e2, losing the right to castle and obstructing development. Black can develop and challenge the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Bb4 d4
explanation.title: Vienna Game: 3. d4 against ...Bb4

explanations.explanation: White pushes d4 to challenge e5, but the c3 knight is pinned to the king. If Black exchanges, bxc3 gives White doubled pawns and central control.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5 Qg4
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Giraffe Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen to attack g7. This exploits the bishop’s departure from f8, but exposes the queen early.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 d6 f4
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Omaha Gambit

explanations.explanation: White attacks e5 with the f-pawn, hoping to build a broad center. The pawn advance also weakens the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 f5
explanation.title: Vienna Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 with the f-pawn. White can capture on f5, opening lines on the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Ne2
explanation.title: Alapin Opening

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to e2, temporarily blocking the f1 bishop. One idea is f4; other continuations can transpose into open games.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5
explanation.title: King’s Knight Opening: Busch-Gass Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and leaves e5 undefended. After Nxe5, Black can play ...Qh4 to create a mating threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Busch-Gass Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn. Black can respond with ...Qh4, threatening f2 and attacking e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4
explanation.title: Busch-Gass Gambit: 3...Qh4

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen threatens f2 alongside the bishop, and also attacks e4. White must meet the threats.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 a3
explanation.title: Mengarini Opening

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn controls b4, limiting a future ...Bb4. White has postponed developing a piece, so Black has several active replies.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 c3
explanation.title: Center Pawn Opening

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 with the c-pawn. This plan can build a broad center, though the pawn occupies the knight’s usual c3 square.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 c4
explanation.title: The Whale: 2. c4

explanations.explanation: White adds control of d5. The move also restricts the f1 bishop and leaves d4 as a potential weakness.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d3
explanation.title: Leonardis Variation

explanations.explanation: White supports e4 and opens a diagonal for the c1 bishop. The d-pawn also blocks the f1 bishop’s diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4
explanation.title: Center Game

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5 immediately. After ...exd4, White can recapture or offer a pawn for rapid development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 d6
explanation.title: Center Game: 2...d6

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5. White can develop Nf3 or exchange pawns and queens, leaving Black’s king unable to castle.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Center Game: 2...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recover it with the queen, prepare Nxd4, or offer a further pawn with c3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Bc4
explanation.title: Center Game: von der Lasa Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 while leaving the d-pawn for the moment. The position can transpose to other open gambits.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Nf3
explanation.title: Center Game: Kieseritzky Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and attacks d4. Black’s developing replies can transpose into a Scotch Game.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4
explanation.title: Center Game: 3. Qxd4

explanations.explanation: White recovers the pawn with the queen and removes Black’s e-pawn from the center. Black can develop ...Nc6 with an attack on the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Qxd4 Nc6
explanation.title: Center Game: 3...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks the queen, gaining time as it retreats. White often chooses Qe3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3
explanation.title: Danish Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the c-pawn as well as the d-pawn, seeking rapid development and open lines. Black can accept with ...dxc3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 d5
explanation.title: Danish Gambit: Sørensen Defense

explanations.explanation: Black counters in the center with ...d5. After exd5 and ...Qxd5, White cannot immediately develop Nc3 because the c-pawn occupies that square.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3
explanation.title: Danish Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn. White can recapture or offer another pawn in exchange for faster development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Bc4
explanation.title: Danish Gambit: Double Pawn Sacrifice

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and offers the b-pawn. If Black captures it, White can develop the other bishop with Bxb2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3
explanation.title: Danish Gambit: 4. Nxc3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight, recovering a pawn while developing. White has an active piece and a central pawn in return for the remaining material deficit.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Falkbeer Countergambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. Black can challenge the center by advancing ...e4 or offering further material with ...c6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 e4
explanation.title: Falkbeer Countergambit: 3...e4
