explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn rather than recapturing. It controls f3, making the knight’s usual development more difficult.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4
explanation.title: King’s Gambit Accepted: Bishop’s Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and clears f1 for the king. Black can check with ...Qh4+, though the queen may later become a target.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4 Qh4
explanation.title: Bishop’s Gambit: 3...Qh4+

explanations.explanation: Black checks along the diagonal to the king. White must respond to check and will lose the right to castle if the king moves.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4 Qh4 Kf1
explanation.title: Bishop’s Gambit: 4. Kf1

explanations.explanation: White moves the king to f1 to escape check, giving up castling. Nf3 can later develop while attacking Black’s queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3
explanation.title: King’s Gambit Accepted: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls h4, preventing ...Qh4+. A later d4 can open the bishop’s line toward the pawn on f4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Bc5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit Accepted: 3...Bc5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop. White can play d4, gaining central space and attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Be7
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Cunningham Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and renews the possibility of ...Bh4+, despite the knight’s control of h4. White must consider how to meet the check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Be7 Bc4
explanation.title: Cunningham Defense: 4. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and clears f1 for the king if Black checks on h4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 Nf6
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Schallopp Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight rather than defending the f4 pawn. The knight pressures e4 and supports central counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Modern Defense

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 and opens a diagonal for the c8 bishop. White can exchange on d5 rather than allow ...dxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Fischer Defense

explanations.explanation: Black controls e5 and opens a diagonal for the c8 bishop. Black delays ...g5 and keeps several continuations available.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 d6 d4
explanation.title: Fischer Defense: 4. d4

explanations.explanation: White builds a central pawn pair and opens the bishop’s line toward f4. Black may defend the pawn with ...g5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: 3...g5

explanations.explanation: Black defends the f4 pawn and threatens ...g4 to attack White’s knight. White can challenge the pawn chain or develop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: 4. Bc4 against ...g5

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and clears f1 for the king if Black later checks with ...Qh4+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 d4
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Rosentreter Gambit

explanations.explanation: White establishes a pawn center and opens the bishop’s line toward f4. Black can advance ...g4 to attack the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: 4. h4

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn attacks g5, challenging Black’s pawn chain. Black can advance the g-pawn to g4 and attack the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 h6
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Becker Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...g5, supporting the f4 pawn. The h-pawn can support that pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 g3
explanation.title: Open Game: 2. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares to fianchetto the bishop on g2. Black can develop actively and put pressure on e4 before White completes the setup.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5
explanation.title: Benoni Defense

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4 from the flank. White often advances d5, gaining space and defining the central pawn structure.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 Nf3
explanation.title: Benoni Defense: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and supports d4, avoiding an immediate d5 advance. Black can exchange on d4 or choose another central plan.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5
explanation.title: Benoni Defense: 3. d5

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn, gaining space and restricting Black. Black can challenge the pawn chain with ...e6 or adopt another setup.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 d6
explanation.title: Old Indian Defense: 2...d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn controls e5 and supports a flexible Indian setup. The position can transpose into a King’s Indian if Black follows with ...g6.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4 and offers the e-pawn. Black seeks active piece play and often recovers the pawn after dxe5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 d5
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit Declined

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn instead of accepting the gambit. Black can develop the bishop to c5, aiming toward f2.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the offered pawn and attacks the knight. Black commonly moves it to g4, preparing to recover the pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 f3
explanation.title: Anti-Grünfeld: 3. f3

explanations.explanation: White prepares e4 to build a broad center. The f-pawn move also weakens the kingside and occupies the knight’s usual square.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 e4
explanation.title: Omega Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the e-pawn for development chances. After ...Nxe4, Bd3 can develop with an attack on the knight.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 f3
explanation.title: Paleface Attack

explanations.explanation: White prepares e4, seeking a broad center. The f-pawn move also occupies the kingside knight’s usual square and weakens the king’s flank.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 g4
explanation.title: Bronstein Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the g-pawn to deflect the knight from the center. If ...Nxg4, e4 can gain space while attacking that knight.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Krejcik Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 but leaves e4 undefended. Black can capture the pawn with ...Nxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4
explanation.title: Krejcik Variation: 2...Nxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White can sacrifice the bishop with Bxf7+ and try to recover the knight through checks.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and defends e4. Black can transpose to a Vienna Game with ...e5 or challenge the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Nc3 d5
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Scandinavian Variation

explanations.explanation: Black adds a second attack on e4. White can exchange on d5 or advance e5, attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Nc3 d5 e5
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 3. e5 against ...d5

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the knight. After ...Nfd7, the position can transpose into French Defense structures.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Maróczy Variation

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 instead of immediately attacking the knight. The pawn move also opens a diagonal for the c1 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 Nc3
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Sämisch Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops and offers an exchange of knights. After ...Nxc3 and dxc3, White opens lines but cannot support e5 with the d-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Two Pawns Attack

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the knight again. Black commonly retreats it to b6.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4 Nb6
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 3...Nb6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight from the c-pawn’s attack. White can build a larger center with d4 or advance c5 to attack the knight again.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4 Nb6 a4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Tate Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the a-pawn and threatens a5, potentially trapping the knight on b6. Black can prevent the advance or give the knight an escape square.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 c4 Nb6 d4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 4. d4 after 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White builds a broad center with pawns on c4, d4 and e5. Black commonly challenges the advanced e-pawn with ...d6.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White supports e5 and takes more central space. Black can challenge the advanced pawn with ...d6.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 3...d6

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e5 and opens a diagonal for the c8 bishop. White must decide how to support or exchange the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Modern Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops and prepares to recapture on e5 if Black exchanges. Black can resolve the tension or continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 4. c4

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the knight. The pawn on e5 prevents the knight returning to f6.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 g3
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: 3. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares Bg2, placing the bishop on the long diagonal toward the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Ne4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Mokele Mbembe Variation

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight forward rather than retreating to d5. White can build a center with d4 and later attack the knight with f3.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Ng8
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Brooklyn Variation

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight to its starting square. White has gained space with e5, while Black retains options for challenging the center.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: Tennison Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight while offering the e4 pawn. After ...dxe4, Ng5 attacks the advanced pawn and pressures f7.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4
explanation.title: Tennison Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn and attacks the knight. White often moves Ng5 to pressure e4 and f7.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5
explanation.title: Tennison Gambit: 3. Ng5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight attacks e4 and pressures f7. Black can defend the pawn with a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Bc4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: Bowdler Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop early. Black can play ...e6 and later ...d5, challenging the center and attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls d5. White keeps the option of a closed setup rather than committing immediately to d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6
explanation.title: Closed Sicilian: 2...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and controls d4. White can continue with a closed setup or later open the center with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 f4
explanation.title: Closed Sicilian: Grand Prix Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the f-pawn, preparing kingside play rather than immediately exchanging on d4. The pawn also controls e5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3
explanation.title: Closed Sicilian: Fianchetto Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares to develop the bishop on g2. A typical setup also includes Nge2, d3 and castling.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 d6
explanation.title: Closed Sicilian: 2...d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn controls e5 and keeps several setups available. A later ...d5 would take an additional pawn move.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nc3 e6
explanation.title: Closed Sicilian: 2...e6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...d5 and opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop. White can still choose an open Sicilian with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 g6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Rossolimo, 3...g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to fianchetto the bishop on g7 and castle. White must decide whether to exchange the bishop for the knight on c6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 a3
explanation.title: Sicilian: Delayed Mengarini Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares b4, offering a flank pawn to divert Black’s c-pawn. The preparatory a-pawn move delays development.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 b4
explanation.title: Sicilian: Portsmouth Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn to divert Black’s c-pawn from its control of d4 and seek rapid development.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 b4 cxb4
explanation.title: Portsmouth Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the b-pawn. White can continue with d4, using the time spent on the capture to build a center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 c3
explanation.title: Sicilian: Delayed Alapin

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 with the c-pawn, as in the Alapin. Black can challenge the center with ...Nf6 or ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 a6
explanation.title: Sicilian: O’Kelly Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn controls b5, a useful square in many Sicilian lines. Black has spent a second move on a pawn and has yet to develop a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 a6 c4
explanation.title: O’Kelly Variation: 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White’s c-pawn and e-pawn control d5. White can develop Nc3 and build a Maróczy-style setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 Bc4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defense: 3. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and can follow with d3, c3 and castling, choosing a quieter setup than the open Sicilian.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Qxd4
explanation.title: Sicilian: Chekhover Variation

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the queen instead of the knight. The early queen move avoids some main lines but can give Black targets for development.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 c3
explanation.title: Sicilian: Tartakower Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the c-pawn for quicker development and open files. After ...dxc3, Nxc3 reaches a Smith-Morra-like position with ...d6 played.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e5
explanation.title: Sicilian: Jalalabad Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn alongside the c-pawn, but the knight can capture it. Black may seek activity in return.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 b3
explanation.title: Sicilian: 3. b3 against ...e6

explanations.explanation: White prepares to develop the bishop on b2. Black can continue with a standard Sicilian setup or challenge the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Taimanov Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queenside knight while keeping the kingside knight and d-pawn flexible. White commonly develops Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6
explanation.title: Sicilian: 4...Nf6 after ...e6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks e4. White must decide how to meet the threat before Black commits further pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 a6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Kan Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn controls b5 while Black delays choosing a setup for the knights. White can develop or establish a Maróczy bind with c4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 f5
explanation.title: Sicilian: Brussels Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the f-pawn in an attempt to divert White’s e-pawn. The advance also opens diagonals around Black’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6 c4
explanation.title: Hyperaccelerated Dragon: 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White’s c-pawn and e-pawn control d5, preparing a Maróczy bind before developing Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6 d4
explanation.title: Hyperaccelerated Dragon: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White offers the d-pawn to open the center. After ...cxd4, a knight recapture gives White active lines.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6 d4 cxd4
explanation.title: Hyperaccelerated Dragon: 3...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the c-pawn for White’s d-pawn. White can recapture with the knight, gaining open lines while Black retains both central pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 g6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Hyperaccelerated Dragon: 4. Nxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight. Black can develop ...Nc6 and reach an Accelerated Dragon setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 a3 Nc6
explanation.title: Mengarini Variation: 2...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and controls d4. White can proceed with b4, offering the pawn to divert Black’s c-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 a3 Nc6 b4
explanation.title: Mengarini Variation: 3. b4

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn, supported by the a3 pawn. Black can accept with ...cxb4 or develop a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 b4 cxb4
explanation.title: Sicilian Wing Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the b-pawn. White can play a3 to challenge it or continue with d4 to build a center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 b4 cxb4 a3
explanation.title: Sicilian Wing Gambit: 3. a3

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn challenges b4. If Black exchanges on a3, White can recapture with the bishop and develop it.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 b4 cxb4 a3 d5
explanation.title: Sicilian Wing Gambit: 3...d5

explanations.explanation: Black counterattacks e4 rather than resolving the queenside pawn tension. White must consider the central threat before recovering b4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn. White can recapture with Nxc3, developing a piece and opening lines for both bishops.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 4. Nxc3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight, gaining development for the pawn. Nf3, Bc4 and castling are natural continuations.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 4...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and controls d4 and e5. White has rapid development in exchange for the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 bxc3
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 4. bxc3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the b-pawn. This leaves isolated a- and c-pawns and occupies the knight’s usual c3 square, without developing a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 d5 exd5 c6
explanation.title: Falkbeer Countergambit: 3...c6

explanations.explanation: Black offers the c-pawn for development and open lines. White can accept or continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Bc4 Qh4 Ke2
explanation.title: Bishop’s Gambit: 4. Ke2

explanations.explanation: White moves the king out of check, losing castling rights but leaving the f-file available for the rook to use later.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Nf3
explanation.title: Danish Gambit: 4. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight while offering the b-pawn. If Black captures on b2, White can develop the c1 bishop by recapturing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nc6 f4 exf4 d4
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Steinitz Gambit

explanations.explanation: White builds a center with d4 but allows ...Qh4+, which can make the king vulnerable. White seeks development and central play for the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bb5 c6 Ba4
explanation.title: Portuguese Opening: 3. Ba4

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop from the c-pawn’s attack. Black can gain more time with ...b5, attacking it again.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bb5 c6 Ba4 b5
explanation.title: Portuguese Opening: 3...b5

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop for a second time. White can retreat it to b3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 Bc4 Nc6
explanation.title: von der Lasa Gambit: 3...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and defends d4. White can play Nf3, transposing into a Scotch Gambit.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: Modern Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks the pawn on d5, postponing the recapture. This avoids moving the queen out immediately.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4
explanation.title: Modern Scandinavian: 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White defends the d5 pawn. Black can challenge the pawn chain with ...c6 or ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 e6
explanation.title: Modern Scandinavian: Icelandic Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the e-pawn to undermine d5. If White captures it, Black can recapture with the bishop, gaining development.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 c4 e6 dxe6
explanation.title: Icelandic Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn. Black can recapture with the bishop, developing a second minor piece while remaining a pawn down.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4
explanation.title: Modern Scandinavian: 3. d4

explanations.explanation: White claims central space and opens the bishop’s diagonal. Black can recover the pawn on d5 with the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Nf6 d4 Bg4
explanation.title: Modern Scandinavian: Portuguese Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop with an attack on the queen. White must respond while Black seeks active play for the offered pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 Qxd5 c4
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White advances the c-pawn and attacks the queen. The move gains space but delays piece development.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 exd5 c6
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: Blackburne Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the c-pawn to divert White’s pawn from d5. After dxc6, ...Nxc6 recaptures while developing a knight.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 d3
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: 2. d3

explanations.explanation: White supports e4, but after ...dxe4 the d-pawn is pinned to the queen. Recapturing then allows a queen exchange.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 e5
explanation.title: Scandinavian Defense: 2. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn to gain space. Black can develop the light-squared bishop before playing ...e6, reaching a French-like structure.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 Bf5
explanation.title: Tennison Gambit: 3...Bf5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and defends e4. White can develop Nc3 to add pressure on the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 Bf5 Nc3
explanation.title: Tennison Gambit: 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and adds another attack on e4. Black can defend the pawn with ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 Nf6
explanation.title: Tennison Gambit: 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and defends e4. White can challenge the pawn again with d3 or continue development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 Nf6 cxd5
explanation.title: Marshall Defense: 3. cxd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. After ...Nxd5, e4 can gain time by attacking the knight; after ...Qxd5, Nc3 can attack the queen.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit: Austrian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black mirrors the c-pawn with ...c5, creating tension around both central pawns.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c5 cxd5 Nf6
explanation.title: Austrian Defense: Gusev Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight instead of immediately recovering the pawn on d5, offering a pawn for activity.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops a knight and controls e4. White can develop Nf3 and maintain the tension in the center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Defense

explanations.explanation: Black reinforces d5, accepting that the light-squared bishop is temporarily behind the pawn chain. Black can seek ...e5 or ...c5 later.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 3...dxc4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn and can try to hold it with ...b5. The advance may also attack White’s knight on c3.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4 e3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 4. e3 after ...dxc4

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 and opens the bishop’s line toward c4. The c3 knight retains e4 as a retreat.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4 e3 b5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 4...b5

explanations.explanation: Black defends c4 and may advance ...b4 to attack the knight. White can challenge the pawn chain.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4 e4
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Alekhine Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances e4, gaining space and opening the bishop’s line to c4. Black often supports the extra pawn with ...b5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 e5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Winawer Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the e-pawn to challenge White’s center. After dxe5, ...d4 can attack the knight and gain space.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bf5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Schallopp Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain. The knight helps defend d5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 e3 Bg4
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Pin Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the f3 knight to the queen. White can question the bishop with h3.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3
explanation.title: Exchange Slav: 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and pressures d5, keeping several setups available. Black can develop ...Nf6 to reinforce the pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 cxd5 cxd5 Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: Exchange Slav: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and supports d5. White can develop the bishop to f4 or continue with Nf3.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nc3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, but Black can attack it with a later ...b5 and ...b4 while trying to hold the c4 pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 4...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens the f8 bishop’s diagonal. White can recover the pawn with Bxc4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 4. a4

explanations.explanation: White attacks b5, challenging Black’s attempt to hold the c4 pawn. Black can support b5 with ...c6.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4 c6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 4...c6

explanations.explanation: Black supports b5 and holds the queenside pawn chain for now. White can capture on b5 to challenge it.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Be7
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Charousek Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, discouraging Bg5 because the bishop can be exchanged. White can continue developing with Nf3.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Nbd7
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 4...Nbd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queenside knight and can prepare a Cambridge Springs setup with ...c6 and ...Qa5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 c5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Semi-Tarrasch

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4. After cxd5, Black can recapture with the knight, avoiding an isolated d-pawn at the cost of allowing White central space.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 dxc4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Vienna Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn, giving up some central control. White can advance e4 and build a broad center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. After ...exd5 the Carlsbad structure offers White several plans, including queenside pawn play.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 cxd5 exd5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 4...exd5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures and opens a diagonal for the light-squared bishop. The resulting Carlsbad pawn structure shapes both sides’ plans.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5
explanation.title: Tarrasch Defense: 4. cxd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. Black can recapture with the e-pawn or offer the Schara Gambit with ...cxd4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5 cxd4
explanation.title: Tarrasch Defense: Schara Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black captures on d4, offering a pawn for rapid development. If White takes with the queen, ...Nc6 develops while attacking it.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 Nf3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 4. Nf3 against ...c6

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can enter the Semi-Slav with ...Nf6 or capture on c4 in the Noteboom Variation.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 Nf3 dxc4
explanation.title: Noteboom Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures the c-pawn, seeking to hold it with queenside pawns. White can challenge that plan with a4 or develop toward recovery.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Marshall Gambit

explanations.explanation: White builds a broad center with e4 and d4. White may offer a pawn to exploit Black’s undeveloped pieces.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 f5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Stonewall Setup

explanations.explanation: Black advances the f-pawn and controls e4. This Stonewall structure restricts central squares but leaves the light-squared bishop behind its pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 e5 c5 b4
explanation.title: French Defense: Wing Gambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the b-pawn to divert Black’s c-pawn from the center. Black can accept with ...cxb4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Nf3 d5 e5 c5 b4 cxb4
explanation.title: French Wing Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the b-pawn. White can challenge it with a3 and seek open lines for development.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Qe2 c5 Nf3
explanation.title: French Defense: Chigorin, 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight while Black’s c-pawn controls d4. Both sides can continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Qe2 c5 Nf3 Nc6
explanation.title: French Defense: Chigorin, 3...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and adds control of d4. White can play g3 and develop the bishop to g2.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2
explanation.title: French Defense: Winawer, 4. Bd2

explanations.explanation: White interposes the bishop to break the pin on c3. Black can still capture on e4; an immediate Nxe4 then allows ...Qxd4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 dxe4
explanation.title: Winawer: 4...dxe4 after Bd2

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. If White immediately recaptures with the knight, Black’s queen can capture on d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 dxe4 Qg4
explanation.title: Winawer: 5. Qg4

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen with an attack on g7, seeking activity while a pawn down. Black must address the threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Nge2
explanation.title: Winawer: Alekhine Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the kingside knight and leaves e4 exposed. Black can accept the offered pawn with ...dxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Nge2 dxe4
explanation.title: Winawer: Alekhine Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White can seek active play and challenge the bishop on b4 without necessarily accepting doubled c-pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3
explanation.title: Winawer: 5. a3

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn attacks the bishop. Black must choose whether to exchange on c3 or retreat while maintaining central pressure.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 exd5
explanation.title: Winawer: 4. exd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn, entering an exchange structure with Nc3 and ...Bb4 already played. Black can recapture with the e-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Bb4
explanation.title: French Defense: McCutcheon Variation

explanations.explanation: Black pins the c3 knight while White’s bishop pins f6. Both sides have tactical pressure on the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7
explanation.title: French Defense: Classical, 4...Be7

explanations.explanation: Black interposes the bishop, ending the pin on f6. The freed knight threatens e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5
explanation.title: French Defense: Classical, 5. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. Black must move it, commonly to d7.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 dxe4
explanation.title: French Defense: Burn Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures on e4, releasing central tension. White can recapture with Nxe4 while maintaining pressure on f6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Be7
explanation.title: French Defense: Morozevich Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop while postponing the choice of a pawn break. White can develop Ngf3 and maintain central tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 4. e5

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the knight. Black commonly retreats it to d7 and later challenges the pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 4...Nfd7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight from the e-pawn’s attack. White retains c3 as a way to support the central pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 5. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward Black’s kingside and clears e2 for the other knight. Black seeks ways to challenge the pawns on d4 and e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 Ngf3
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: Euwe-Keres Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and defends d4, preserving central tension. Black can exchange on d4 or develop.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 c5 exd5
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 4. exd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn, resolving part of the central tension. Black can recapture with either the e-pawn or queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 3...dxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White can recapture with Nxe4, transposing into a Rubinstein position.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nf3
explanation.title: French Defense: Perseus Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and offers the e4 pawn. After ...dxe4, the knight is attacked and must move.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 Bd7
explanation.title: French Advance: 3...Bd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the light-squared bishop with an idea of later exchanging it on b5, relieving the constraint of the pawn chain.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 Qg4
explanation.title: French Advance: Nimzowitsch Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen early. The bishop on f8 still protects g7, so White must build further pressure rather than assume an immediate threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Bd3
explanation.title: French Exchange: 4. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop. Black can mirror with ...Bd6 or challenge the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Be3
explanation.title: French Exchange: 4. Be3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and clears a route for queenside castling. Black can continue development with ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 Nf3
explanation.title: French Exchange: 4. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and prepares kingside castling. Black can respond in kind with ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 c4
explanation.title: French Exchange: Monte Carlo Variation

explanations.explanation: White challenges d5 with the c-pawn. This gains space but leaves White’s d4 pawn without c-pawn support.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5 exd5 c4 Nf6
explanation.title: Monte Carlo Variation: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and defends d5, maintaining the central tension rather than exchanging on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 f5
explanation.title: French Defense: Kingston Defense

explanations.explanation: Black advances the f-pawn and attacks e4. White can capture on f5 or advance e5, changing the central structure.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 c4 d5 exd5 cxd5 cxd5
explanation.title: Accelerated Panov: 4. cxd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the pawn and remains a pawn ahead for now. Black can recover immediately with the queen or develop ...Nf6 first.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 c4 d5 exd5 cxd5 cxd5 Nf6
explanation.title: Accelerated Panov: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks d5. White can develop Nc3 or check with the queen or bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 c4 d5 exd5 cxd5 cxd5 Nf6 Qa4
explanation.title: Accelerated Panov: 5. Qa4+

explanations.explanation: White gives check with the queen. Black must block or otherwise answer the check while considering the attack on b7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Dinic Gambit

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight toward f7 and offers the d3 pawn. After ...exd3, Bxd3 develops with an attack.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 Na6 c4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: De Bruycker, 3. c4

explanations.explanation: White gains central space and controls d5. Black can reposition the knight from a6 or continue kingside development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Mieses, 4. Bxe4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the bishop. Black can develop ...Nf6 with an attack on it.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Nf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Mieses, 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks the bishop. White can retreat to f3 and maintain pressure along the long diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Nf6 Bf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Mieses, 5. Bf3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop and keeps it on the long diagonal. The bishop also controls g4, supporting possible kingside expansion.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Bc4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Von Hennig Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 while offering the e-pawn. Black can continue development with ...Nf6 or ...Bf5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Bd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 5. Bd3 after ...Bf5

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop but leaves d4 undefended by the queen. Black can capture the pawn with ...Qxd4, after which Nf3 attacks the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Karpov Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, preparing to exchange White’s centralized knight without committing the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Tartakower Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops and offers an exchange of knights. White can capture on f6, leaving Black a choice of pawn recaptures.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Tartakower, 5. Nxf6

explanations.explanation: White exchanges the knight on f6. Black can recapture with the e-pawn or g-pawn, creating different pawn structures.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Qc7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 4...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen early with an idea of preparing ...e5. White can continue development with Bc4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 e5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 4...e5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4, offering the pawn. After dxe5, ...Qxd1+ can force White’s king to move.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 4...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop but confines the c8 bishop. White can develop Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 f6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 4...f6

explanations.explanation: Black’s f-pawn prepares ...e5. It also weakens the kingside and occupies the knight’s usual f6 square.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 g6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 4...g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the bishop on g7 without immediately challenging White’s knight on e4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 h6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Finnish Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the h-pawn, providing h7 as a possible retreat for the c8 bishop later. White can develop Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 4...Bxd3

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges bishops on d3. White can recapture with the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 5. Qxd3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the queen. Black can develop and support the center with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: Black supports d5. White can play g4 to question the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nd2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 4. Nd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, keeping c3 available for the c-pawn. The knight can later head toward b3 and c5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 4...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and adds pressure on d4. White can develop Nf3 to reinforce it.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 5. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops and supports d4. Black can exchange on d4 to resolve the tension.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 cxd4
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 4...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recapture with the c-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 4. dxc5

explanations.explanation: White captures the c-pawn. Black can develop ...Nc6 or open the bishop’s diagonal with ...e6 to target White’s pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 Nc6
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 4...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks e5. White is a pawn ahead but must defend the advanced pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 e6
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls Defense: 4...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens the bishop’s line toward c5. White can defend the extra pawn with Be3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 4...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks d4. White commonly supports the pawn with c3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 5. c3

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 and keeps a solid pawn structure. The bishop on d3 contests f5 and g6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6
explanation.title: Panov Attack: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and supports d5. White commonly develops Nc3 to add pressure on the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3
explanation.title: Panov Attack: 5. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and adds pressure on d5. Black can support the center with ...e6 or develop ...Nc6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 4...e5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4 and opens a queen check on h4. White can develop Nf3 while addressing the threat.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and pressures d5. Black can pin the knight with ...Bb4 or develop ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 4...Bb4

explanations.explanation: Black pins the knight to the king. White can choose between several developing setups.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 5. Bf4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop while the c3 knight remains pinned. Black can develop ...Ne7 and consider how to activate the c8 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Ne2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 5. Ne2

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, adding support to c3 and d4. Black can continue with ...Ne7 or ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7
explanation.title: Italian Game: Jerome Gambit

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the bishop on f7, drawing Black’s king out. Black can accept with ...Kxf7, leaving White to seek an attack for the material.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7 Kxf7
explanation.title: Jerome Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the bishop with the king. White can continue checking and attacking, but has sacrificed a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Nxe5
explanation.title: Jerome Gambit: 5. Nxe5+

explanations.explanation: White captures on e5 with check, offering another piece. If Black captures the knight, White can use d4 or Qh5+ to try to recover material.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 O-O Nf6 d4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Deutz Gambit

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5 after castling. The advance opens the center and offers a pawn for active play.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bb6
explanation.title: Evans Gambit Declined

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop instead of capturing b4. White can advance a4 and later a5 to challenge the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bb6 b5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit Declined: 5. b5

explanations.explanation: White’s b-pawn attacks the knight, attempting to divert it from defending e5. Black can reply ...Na5, attacking the bishop on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bb6 b5 Na5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit Declined: 5...Na5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight and attacks the bishop. White can consider capturing the now undefended e5 pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Bc5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: 5...Bc5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop. White can play d4, attacking the bishop and contesting e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Bd6
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: 5...Bd6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop and defends e5. The bishop also blocks the d-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Be7
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Anderssen Variation

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop to safety. White can play d4, building a center and attacking e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Bf8
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Mayet Defense

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop to its starting square. White can use the time to advance d4 and contest the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 d5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Hein Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn attacks the bishop and also challenges e4, declining the offered b-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Center Attack

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5, supported by the c3 pawn. Black can exchange on d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Italian Center Attack: 5...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures on d4. White can recapture with cxd4 or advance e5 to attack the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 Nf6
explanation.title: Giuoco Pianissimo: 4...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, pressuring e4 and preparing kingside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 f5
explanation.title: Giuoco Pianissimo: Lucchini Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black advances the f-pawn and attacks e4, breaking the quiet symmetry and offering the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 f5 Ng5
explanation.title: Lucchini Gambit: 5. Ng5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight pressures f7, joining the bishop. Black must consider the tactical threats.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4
explanation.title: Italian Gambit

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5, offering the d-pawn to open lines and accelerate development. Black has several ways to capture it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4
explanation.title: Italian Gambit: 4...Nxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn with the knight. White can take the undefended e5 pawn and create threats against f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5
explanation.title: Italian Gambit: 5. Nxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn. The knight and bishop both pressure f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7
explanation.title: Italian Gambit: 5...Qe7

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks the knight and the e4 pawn behind it. Moving the queen also avoids a knight fork on f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Be7
explanation.title: Italian Game: Hungarian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to a restrained square, keeping a compact position and preparing kingside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Blackburne Shilling Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight to d4 and leaves e5 exposed. After Nxe5, ...Qg5 can attack both the knight and g2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5
explanation.title: Blackburne Shilling Gambit: 4. Nxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn, but Black can play ...Qg5, attacking both the knight and g2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5
explanation.title: Blackburne Shilling Gambit: 4...Qg5

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks the knight and g2 at the same time.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5 O-O
explanation.title: Blackburne Shilling Gambit: 5. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, moving the king to safety and defending g2 with the rook. Black can capture the knight on e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 5. Bxf7+

explanations.explanation: White captures on f7 with check, choosing a different line from the immediate knight capture. Black must move the king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 5...Ke7

explanations.explanation: Black moves the king out of check. The king can no longer castle, but Black retains counterattacking chances.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 5...Bxf2+

explanations.explanation: Black captures on f2 with check, pursuing a counterattack despite White’s knight fork on f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 d4
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 5. d4

explanations.explanation: White’s d-pawn attacks the bishop instead of capturing on f7. This also opens a line for White’s c1 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Nd5
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 4...Nd5

explanations.explanation: Black places the knight on d5 to meet the attack on f7. Moving it also opens the queen’s attack on the g5 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Nd5 d4
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5. d4 against ...Nd5

explanations.explanation: White advances d4, opening the bishop’s defense of the g5 knight and challenging Black’s center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Nxe4 Bxf7
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5. Bxf7+ against ...Nxe4

explanations.explanation: White captures on f7 with check, forcing the king to respond and disrupting Black’s coordination.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nb4
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: Kloss Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight to b4, adding pressure to d5 while offering material for activity.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nd4
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: Fritz Variation

explanations.explanation: Black places the knight centrally, attacking c2 and offering tactical play. The knight can itself be challenged by White’s pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Ne7
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5...Ne7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight and adds pressure on d5. White can develop Nc3 to defend the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 4...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can castle or advance e5, gaining time against the f6 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1 and bringing the rook toward the e-file. White has offered a pawn for active play.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Bc5
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5...Bc5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and defends d4. White can advance e5, entering Max Lange attacking lines.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Nxe4
explanation.title: Scotch Gambit: 5...Nxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White can use the open e-file to create pressure against the knight and king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5. e5

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks the knight. Black must choose a retreat while White keeps central initiative.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 d6
explanation.title: Italian Game: Paris Defense

explanations.explanation: Black reinforces e5, but the d-pawn restricts the f8 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 d6 Nc3
explanation.title: Paris Defense: 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and supports e4, continuing development without committing the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 d6 Nc3 Bg4
explanation.title: Paris Defense: 4...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the knight to the queen. White can question the bishop with h3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 f5
explanation.title: Italian Game: Rousseau Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 with the f-pawn, offering it for counterplay. White can defend e4 or accept on f5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 f5 d3
explanation.title: Rousseau Gambit Declined

explanations.explanation: White supports e4, declining the offered f-pawn. Both sides can continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 f5 exf5
explanation.title: Rousseau Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the f-pawn. Black can seek active play and recover material while White completes development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 h6
explanation.title: Italian Game: Anti-Fried Liver Defense

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn controls g5, preventing an immediate Ng5. Black can prepare to develop the f6 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 3...Nxe4 after Bc4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White must consider the exposed bishop and central counterplay before taking e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Nc3
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Boden-Kieseritzky Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and attacks the knight on e4. If Black exchanges, dxc3 opens a diagonal for White’s bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Bb4
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 3...Bb4 after Nc3

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, attacking c3. White can capture the e5 pawn while e4 remains defended by the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight. Black can recapture with the d-pawn, opening lines for the queen and bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 4...dxc6

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures with the d-pawn, opening the d-file and a diagonal for the c8 bishop. Black seeks activity for the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 Nc3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and defends e4. Black can develop the bishop to c5 and aim at f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 Nc3 Bc5
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5...Bc5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop toward f2. A later ...Ng4 can add another attacker to that square.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5. d3

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and opens the c1 bishop’s diagonal. Black often develops ...Bc5, pressuring f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5...Bc5 after d3

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop toward f2 and may try ...Ng4 to add pressure. White must consider the threat while developing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 e5
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. Black must move it and can look for active squares.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 f3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5. f3

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and controls g4, restricting the black knight. The move also weakens White’s kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 d4
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit Declined

explanations.explanation: White plays d4, building a pawn center instead of exchanging knights immediately. Black can recover the pawn and develop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 4. Qe2

explanations.explanation: White’s queen attacks the knight and lines up with the black king along the e-file. Black must respond carefully.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Qe7
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Kholmov Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black places the queen on e7, allowing Qxe4 but preparing pressure along the e-file. White can capture the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Qe7 Qxe4
explanation.title: Kholmov Gambit: 5. Qxe4

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight. Black’s queen pins the e5 knight to White’s queen and can prepare to recover material.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Qe7 Qxe4 d6
explanation.title: Kholmov Gambit: 5...d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn attacks the pinned knight. White can play d4 before the exchanges.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d5
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 3...d5

explanations.explanation: Black offers the d-pawn for activity instead of immediately recovering e5. White can accept with exd5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Cochrane Gambit

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7, drawing Black’s king out in exchange for material and attacking chances.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7
explanation.title: Cochrane Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the knight with the king. White must use the exposed king and central pawns to generate play for the sacrificed piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7 d4
explanation.title: Cochrane Gambit: 5. d4

explanations.explanation: White builds a central pawn pair with d4 and e4, seeking activity against the exposed black king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 d4 exd4 e5
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: 4. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the pawn and attacks the knight. Black must find a square for it while White seeks to recover the pawn on d4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 Nc6 Nc3 e6
explanation.title: Black Knights’ Tango: 3...e6 after Nc3

explanations.explanation: Black supports d5 and opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 Nc6 Nf3 e6
explanation.title: Black Knights’ Tango: 3...e6 after Nf3

explanations.explanation: Black opens the bishop’s diagonal while keeping a flexible central setup. A later ...Bb4 can transpose into Indian defenses.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 Ne4
explanation.title: Benoni Defense: Vulture Variation

explanations.explanation: Black places the knight on e4, aiming to control central squares and potentially reroute to d6.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5
explanation.title: Benko Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the b-pawn to gain queenside activity and open files. White can accept with cxb5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5
explanation.title: Benko Gambit: 4. cxb5

explanations.explanation: White accepts the b-pawn. Black often continues ...a6, offering another pawn to open queenside lines.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6
explanation.title: Benko Gambit: 4...a6

explanations.explanation: Black offers the a-pawn. After bxa6, Black can recover one pawn and seek activity on the queenside files.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 cxb5 a6 bxa6
explanation.title: Benko Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the a-pawn. Black can recapture with the bishop, developing it and pressuring the center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 e6
explanation.title: Modern Benoni

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d5, aiming for an unbalanced pawn structure and active counterplay.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ne4
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: Fajarowicz Variation

explanations.explanation: Black centralizes the knight instead of immediately attacking the e5 pawn, seeking rapid piece activity.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ne4 Nf3
explanation.title: Fajarowicz Variation: 4. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops and controls d2, helping meet checks on the diagonal. Black can continue with ...Nc6 or ...Bb4+.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ne4 Qc2
explanation.title: Fajarowicz Variation: 4. Qc2

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen and attacks the knight, choosing a square where Black cannot easily attack it while developing.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ne4 a3
explanation.title: Fajarowicz Variation: 4. a3

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn controls b4, discouraging bishop checks and knight jumps there. White can prepare Qc2 against the e4 knight.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: 3...Ng4

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight and attacks e5. White can defend the extra pawn or return it while developing.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: Rubinstein Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop outside the pawn chain and can support e5 with e3. Black can continue developing.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Nf3
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: Adler Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and is prepared to return the e5 pawn in exchange for active development.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Nf3 Nc6
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: 4...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and adds pressure on e5, delaying the choice of a square for the f8 bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Bg5
explanation.title: Neo-Indian Attack

explanations.explanation: White’s bishop pins the knight to the queen. The setup resembles a Torre Attack with the c-pawn already advanced.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: Leningrad Variation

explanations.explanation: White pins the f6 knight while Black’s bishop pins the c3 knight. Both sides contest central squares through their pieces.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5 h6
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: Leningrad, 4...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the bishop. White can retreat or exchange on f6.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5 h6 Bh4
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: Leningrad, 5. Bh4

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop, preserving the pin. Black can consider ...g5, though it weakens the kingside.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qb3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: 4. Qb3

explanations.explanation: White’s queen defends c3 and attacks the bishop. Black must decide how to respond.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: Sämisch, 4...Bxc3+

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the bishop for the knight with check. White recaptures with the b-pawn, gaining the bishop pair but doubled c-pawns.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 Bb4
explanation.title: Bogo-Indian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop with check. White must block the check, with Bd2 and Nc3 leading to different structures.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6
explanation.title: Queen’s Indian Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to fianchetto the queenside bishop, contesting the center from a distance.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nf3 b6 g3
explanation.title: Queen’s Indian: 4. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares Bg2, contesting the long diagonal against Black’s planned queenside fianchetto.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 g3 Bb4
explanation.title: Bogo-Catalan Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop with check. White must block, choosing whether to enter a Nimzo-Indian-like position or another Catalan setup.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Bc5 Na4
explanation.title: Vienna Game: 3. Na4

explanations.explanation: White’s knight attacks the bishop, but Black can sacrifice on f2 with check and create complications.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7
explanation.title: Vienna Game: 4. Bxf7+

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the bishop on f7. If Black accepts, White can recover the knight while forcing the black king to lose castling rights.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Falkbeer, 4...Nd6

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the bishop and defends f7. White must respond to the attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Falkbeer, 5. Bb3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop, keeping pressure on f7. Black remains a pawn ahead but must complete development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Be7
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Falkbeer, 5...Be7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop. White can recover the e5 pawn with the queen or add another attacker with Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Falkbeer, 5...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and defends e5. The knight on d6 is a key defender of f7 and can become a target.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Bb3 Nc6 Nb5
explanation.title: Vienna Game: Falkbeer, 6. Nb5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight attacks d6, a key defender of f7. Black must consider the threats to the knight and king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Qh5 Nd6 Qxe5
explanation.title: Vienna Game: 5. Qxe5+

explanations.explanation: White recovers the pawn on e5 with check. Black can offer a queen exchange with ...Qe7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4
explanation.title: Vienna Gambit: 4...Nxe4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the pawn and opens the d8–h4 diagonal. White must account for a possible ...Qh4+ while defending the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 d3
explanation.title: Vienna Gambit: 5. d3

explanations.explanation: White’s d-pawn attacks the knight. Black can exchange on c3 or seek active counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 f4 d5 fxe5 Nxe4 d3 Qh4
explanation.title: Vienna Gambit: Würzburger Trap

explanations.explanation: Black checks with the queen. White must respond and be alert to tactics involving the knight on e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Bb4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Alapin Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, mirroring White’s bishop move. White can exchange on c6 or continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nb4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: 3...Nb4

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight again and leaves e5 apparently undefended. White should consider the tactical reply before capturing.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 Bc4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense, 5. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7, delaying castling. Black’s advanced pawn on d4 remains part of the central tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nd4 Nxd4 exd4 O-O
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Bird Defense, 5. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1. Black can develop ...Bc5 to support d4 or play ...c6, attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Bc5 c3
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: Zukertort Gambit

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 but leaves e4 attacked. Black can accept the pawn with ...Nxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: l’Hermet Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the bishop. White can exchange on c6, entering a Berlin endgame after further trades.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 a6
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: Rosenthal Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn attacks the bishop, aiming to remove its pressure on c6 before expanding in the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Ne7 Nxe5
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: Mortimer Trap

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn, but Black can play ...c6, attacking the bishop and opening a queen check on a5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 d3 Ne7 Nxe5 c6
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: 5...c6

explanations.explanation: Black’s c-pawn attacks the bishop and opens the queen’s diagonal toward a5. White must consider the resulting check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Bd6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: 4...Bd6

explanations.explanation: Black’s bishop reinforces e5, but occupies the d-pawn’s usual development square.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Deferred Bird Defense

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight to d4, leaving e5 apparently vulnerable. White should check the tactics before capturing it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 c3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Jaffe Gambit

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 while e4 is attacked. Black can capture with ...Nxe4, so White must play actively to recover the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: 5. d3

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and chooses a quieter central setup, postponing d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Mackenzie Variation

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5 immediately, seeking open central lines before Black castles.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 b5 Bb3 Na5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Norwegian Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the bishop, seeking the bishop pair. White must choose how to respond.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Modern Steinitz Defense

explanations.explanation: Black reinforces e5. The setup supports the center but restricts the f8 bishop for now.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6 c3
explanation.title: Modern Steinitz: 5. c3

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4, aiming to build a broad pawn center. Black can choose among several defensive setups.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6 d4
explanation.title: Modern Steinitz: 5. d4

explanations.explanation: White attacks e5, but Black can play ...b5 with tempo on the bishop and relieve the pin on c6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 f5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Deferred Schliemann

explanations.explanation: Black offers the f-pawn to challenge White’s center. The earlier ...a6 changes the bishop’s position compared with an immediate Schliemann.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O Bg4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez Exchange: 5...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the knight, discouraging Nxe5. White must consider tactical ideas before chasing the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O f6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez Exchange: Gligorić Variation

explanations.explanation: Black defends e5 with the f-pawn. White can strike in the center with d4 while Black completes development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O f6 d4
explanation.title: Gligorić Variation: 6. d4

explanations.explanation: White attacks e5 and opens the center. Black can exchange on d4 or pin the knight with ...Bg4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez Exchange: 5. d4

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5. Black can exchange on d4 to resolve the immediate central tension.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 d4 exd4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez Exchange: 5...exd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recover it with the queen and consider an exchange of queens.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 d6 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Steinitz, 4. d4

explanations.explanation: White adds pressure on e5. Black can exchange on d4 or break the pin on c6 with ...Bd7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 5. Nxe4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight. Black can develop ...Nf6 or challenge the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 Nf6
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks the knight. White can exchange on f6 or defend the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qe2
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 6. Qe2

explanations.explanation: White’s queen defends the knight. Black can challenge the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 5...d5

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn attacks the knight and claims central space. White has tactical options including Nxe5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 4. d3

explanations.explanation: White defends e4 and also threatens to take the f5 pawn. Black can exchange on e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3 fxe4 dxe4
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 5. dxe4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures the pawn on e4. Black can develop ...Nf6, attacking it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3 fxe4 dxe4 Nf6
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks e4. White can castle while considering the tactics around the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d3 fxe4 dxe4 Nf6 O-O
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 6. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1 and bringing the rook toward the center. Black can continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 d4
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 4. d4

explanations.explanation: White counterattacks e5. Black can exchange on e4, creating sharp central play.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 exf5
explanation.title: Schliemann Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the f-pawn. Black can gain time with ...e4, attacking White’s knight and seeking to recover material.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f6 O-O Bc5 c3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Nürnberg Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 after castling. Black’s bishop on c5 pressures f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 h6
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: 3...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn controls g5, discouraging a future Bg5. Black has delayed piece development.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 c5 d5 b5 g4
explanation.title: Benko Gambit: Mutkin Countergambit

explanations.explanation: White offers the g-pawn and can seek central space with e4 or attack the f6 knight with g5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 g5
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: 4...g5

explanations.explanation: Black’s g-pawn attacks the bishop. The advance gains time but weakens Black’s kingside.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 e4
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: Alekhine Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, claiming central space while the pawn on e5 remains under attack.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 f3 d5
explanation.title: Anti-Grünfeld: 3...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges c4 and contests the center in Grünfeld style. White must prepare e4 carefully because it is under pressure.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 h4
