explanations.explanation: White exchanges on f6. Black can recapture with the queen, developing it while recovering the piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Nxe5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Jerome Gambit: 5...Nxe5

explanations.explanation: Black captures the knight. White can check with Qh5+ and seek to recover a piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Nxe5 Nxe5 Qh5
explanation.title: Jerome Gambit: 6. Qh5+

explanations.explanation: White checks the king on f7 and attacks the knight on e5. Black must respond to the check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bb6 b5 Na5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit Declined: 6. Nxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn, attacking f7 and defending the bishop on c4. Black can seek active replies.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 b4
explanation.title: Italian Game: Dubov Gambit

explanations.explanation: White’s b-pawn attacks the bishop, offering the d4 pawn for development and open lines.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 f5 Ng5 f4
explanation.title: Lucchini Gambit: Dubois Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances f4, opening the queen’s attack on the knight. White must account for the threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d3 f5 Ng5 f4 Bf7
explanation.title: Lucchini Gambit: 6. Bxf7+

explanations.explanation: White captures on f7 with check. Black must move the king while White’s g5 knight is exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Bxf7
explanation.title: Italian Gambit: 6. Bxf7+

explanations.explanation: White captures on f7 with check, forcing Black’s king to respond while the e5 knight remains under attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7
explanation.title: Italian Gambit: 6. Nxf7

explanations.explanation: White’s knight captures on f7 and attacks Black’s rook. Black can exploit the exposed position and White’s loose knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5 Nxf7 Qxg2 Rf1
explanation.title: Blackburne Shilling: 6. Rf1

explanations.explanation: White moves the rook away from attack, but Black can check on e4 and continue the attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 6. Bd5

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop to d5, reinforcing e4 and keeping the possibility of Bxc6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 6. Kf1

explanations.explanation: White moves the king out of check without taking the bishop. Both sides retain tactical threats.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 d4 d5 Bxd5
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 6. Bxd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. Black can recapture with a knight and seek activity despite being a pawn down.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Nxe4 Bxf7 Ke7
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 5...Ke7

explanations.explanation: Black moves the king out of check. White must address the threat of ...Nxg5 and maintain the initiative.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 6. Bb5+

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop with check, escaping the a5 knight’s attack while forcing Black to respond.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 d3
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 6. d3

explanations.explanation: White controls e4 and opens the c1 bishop’s diagonal. Black can capture the bishop on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nd4 d6
explanation.title: Two Knights: Fritz, 6. d6

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn, opening the bishop’s diagonal to f7. Black can capture the pawn with the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxf7
explanation.title: Fried Liver Attack

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7, seeking to draw Black’s king into the open and gain time for an attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Nxd5 d4
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: Lolli Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn, opening the center and pursuing an alternative to the immediate Fried Liver sacrifice.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 b5 Bf1
explanation.title: Two Knights Defense: 6. Bf1

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop to defend g2. If Black captures d5 with the queen, White can develop Nc3 with tempo.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Bc5 e5
explanation.title: Scotch Gambit: Max Lange Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight, gaining space and initiating a sharp attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Nxe4 Nc3
explanation.title: Scotch Gambit: Nakhmanson Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight while offering material for rapid development and activity against Black’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 d4 exd4 O-O Nxe4 Re1
explanation.title: Scotch Gambit: 6. Re1

explanations.explanation: White’s rook pins the knight to the king. Black can respond with ...d5 to challenge the bishop and unblock the position.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 d4 Nxe4 d5 Bc5
explanation.title: Ponziani: Vuković Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop toward f2, offering the c6 knight for an attack. The e4 knight also pressures f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Trébuchet Gambit

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the bishop on f7 with check, seeking to draw Black’s king into the open.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 Ng4
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Vladimir Variation

explanations.explanation: Black moves the knight again, seeking active play but spending another tempo on the same piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 6. Be2

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and controls g4, restricting the black knight and adding defense to the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Nc3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 6. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, but Black can play ...Ng4, adding pressure to f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 e5 Ne4
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 5...Ne4

explanations.explanation: Black centralizes the knight, aiming toward f2 and setting tactical problems for White.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 e5 Ne4 d3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 6. d3

explanations.explanation: White’s d-pawn attacks the knight, but Black can develop ...Bc5 and create threats against f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 e5 Ne4 f3
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 6. f3

explanations.explanation: White’s f-pawn attacks the knight, but opens a diagonal for ...Qh4+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxf7
explanation.title: Stafford Gambit: 4. Nxf7

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7, seeking an attack against Black’s king after ...Kxf7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nxe4 Qe2 Nf6
explanation.title: Petrov Defense: Copycat Trap

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, but the queen on e2 pins the e4 knight. White can win material with a discovered attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7 Bc4
explanation.title: Cochrane Gambit: 5. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward Black’s exposed king. Black can challenge the bishop and center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7 d4 g6
explanation.title: Cochrane Gambit: 5...g6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...Bg7, seeking a defensive setup for the exposed king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Qf6 Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and prepares to castle. Black’s queen occupies f6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 c5 Nxe5 f6
explanation.title: Open Game: 3...f6 after ...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the knight but weakens the diagonal to the king. White can check with Qh5+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 c5 Nxe5 f6 Qh5
explanation.title: Open Game: 4. Qh5+ after ...f6

explanations.explanation: White checks the king along the diagonal. If Black blocks with ...g6, Nxg6 creates a tactical attack on h8.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 c5 Nxe5 f6 Qh5 g6
explanation.title: Open Game: 4...g6 after Qh5+

explanations.explanation: Black blocks the check with the g-pawn. White can play Nxg6, exploiting the alignment with the rook on h8.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 c6 Nxe5 Nf6 d3
explanation.title: Gunderam Gambit: 4. d3

explanations.explanation: White controls e4, but Black can check with ...Qa5+ and fork the king and knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 c6 g3
explanation.title: Gunderam Gambit: 3. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares Bg2 while leaving Black’s e5 pawn under attack. Black can continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Be7 dxe5 dxe5 Qd5
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: 6. Qd5

explanations.explanation: White’s queen joins the bishop in threatening f7. Black must meet the mating threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Ngf6 dxe5 dxe5 Ng5
explanation.title: Philidor Defense: 6. Ng5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight adds pressure on f7, joining the bishop on c4. Black must deal with the tactical threat.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Bc4 fxe4 Nxe5 Qg5 Nf7 Qxg2 Rf1
explanation.title: Latvian Gambit: Mayet, 6. Rf1

explanations.explanation: White moves the rook away from the queen’s attack. Black can strike in the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 f5 Nxe5 Qf6 Nc4 fxe4 Nc3 Qf7 Ne3
explanation.title: Latvian Gambit: Leonhardt, 6. Ne3

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight to contest d5 and attack e4. Black must decide how to support the advanced pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 Bc5 fxe5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit Declined: 3. fxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures the e-pawn, but Black can check with ...Qh4+ and exploit the weakened king position.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 Bc5 fxe5 Qh4 Ke2
explanation.title: King’s Gambit Declined: 4. Ke2

explanations.explanation: White moves the king out of check, but Black can mate with ...Qxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Kf2
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Tumbleweed Gambit

explanations.explanation: White moves the king into an exposed position and loses castling rights. Black can develop with checks.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4 g4 O-O gxf3 Qxf3
explanation.title: Muzio Gambit: 6. Qxf3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the queen and attacks f4. White has sacrificed a knight for development and attacking chances.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 Nf6
explanation.title: Kieseritzky Gambit: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks e4. White can play d4 to challenge Black’s pawn on f4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 d6 Nxg4
explanation.title: Kieseritzky Gambit: 6. Nxg4

explanations.explanation: White captures the g-pawn. Black can develop ...Nf6 and seek activity against the centralized knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Qf3
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Breyer Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen while a pawn down. Black can check with ...Qh4+, though White can block with g3.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 f5
explanation.title: King’s Gambit: Panteldakis Countergambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 and offers the f-pawn, seeking counterplay in the center.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 c4 d5 exd5 cxd5 cxd5 Nf6 Qa4 Bd7
explanation.title: Accelerated Panov: 5...Bd7

explanations.explanation: Black blocks the check with the bishop. White can retreat the queen to b3 and continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 exd3 Bxd3 Nf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Dinic: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, but White can fork the queen and rook with Nf7, supported by the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 exd3 Bxd3 h6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Dinic: 5...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the knight, but White can play Nf7, forking the queen and rook.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Nf6 Bf3 Bf5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Mieses: 5...Bf5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop outside the pawn chain before ...e6. White can continue development while considering the bishop’s exposed position.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Ng5 h6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Karpov: 5...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the knight. White can consider Ne6, exploiting the open diagonal near Black’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Qe2 Ngf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Karpov: 5...Ngf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, but White can mate with Nd6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Ng5 h6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Tartakower: 5...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the knight. White can retreat it to f3 or examine tactical alternatives.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6 exf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Korchnoi Variation

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on f6 with the e-pawn. The pawn structure changes, and Black opens a diagonal for the light-squared bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Nxf6 gxf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Bronstein-Larsen Variation

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on f6 with the g-pawn, accepting an altered kingside pawn structure in return for active possibilities.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qd3 e5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Tartakower: 5...e5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4, opening the position. White can develop while Black must account for the exposed center.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 5...Nd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can consider e6, disrupting Black’s central pawns and gaining space.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 5...e6

explanations.explanation: Black supports d5 after the bishop exchange. White can develop while considering Black’s ...c5 break.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls: 5...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recapture with cxd4, restoring the central pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 e6 Be3 Nh6
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls: 5...Nh6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, planning to reroute it toward f5. White can continue development while defending c5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and can next consider ...Bg4. White often develops the c1 bishop to f4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Qc7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 5...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen controls f4 and influences e5. White must consider the bishop’s development and Black’s central plans.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
explanation.title: Panov Attack: 5...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and pressures d4. White can develop Nf3 or Bg5 while maintaining pressure on d5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 Bg4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 5...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the knight to the queen. White can develop Bc4 toward f7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Ne2 Ne7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Fantasy: 5...Ne7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can play a3 to question the bishop pin on c3.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 dxe4 Qg4 Nf6
explanation.title: French Winawer: 5...Nf6 after Qg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks the queen, allowing Qxg7 but seeking counterplay on the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 Bd2 dxe4 Qg4 Qxd4
explanation.title: French Winawer: Kunin Double Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn with the queen while leaving g7 attacked. White can develop rapidly and exploit Black’s exposed queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Ba5
explanation.title: French Winawer: 5...Ba5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop and keeps the pin on c3. White can advance b4 to challenge it.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5 Nfd7
explanation.title: French Classical: 5...Nfd7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight from the e-pawn’s attack. White can exchange bishops on e7 or play h4 for attacking chances.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 5...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4. White can support the base of the pawn chain with c3.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Qb6 Nf3 Bd7
explanation.title: French Advance: Wade Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop with an idea of exchanging it for White’s bishop. The maneuver takes time but addresses the c8 bishop’s limited scope.

explanation.moves: e4 Nc6 d4 d5 Nc3 a6 exd5 Nb4
explanation.title: Nimzowitsch Defense: 4...Nb4

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight adds pressure on d5. White can develop Bc4 to reinforce the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 Nc6 d4 d5 Nc3 a6 exd5 Nb4 Bc4
explanation.title: Nimzowitsch Defense: 5. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and supports d5. Black can develop ...Nf6 to attack it again.

explanation.moves: e4 Nc6 d4 d5 Nc3 a6 exd5 Nb4 Bc4 Nf6
explanation.title: Nimzowitsch Defense: 5...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and adds another attack on d5. White must decide how to continue development and handle the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 Nc6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 d5 Ne5
explanation.title: Nimzowitsch Defense: 4...Ne5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight from the d-pawn’s attack. White can capture e4 with the other knight or choose a more active continuation.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qh5 Ke6 Qg4
explanation.title: Alekhine Krejcik: 5. Qg4+

explanations.explanation: White checks the king on e6 and attacks the e4 knight, seeking to recover material.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qh5 Kf6 Qf3

explanations.explanation: White checks the king on f6 and attacks e4. Black must answer the check while the knight is exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qh5 Kg8 Qd5
explanation.title: Alekhine Krejcik: 5. Qd5+ against ...Kg8

explanations.explanation: White checks the king and attacks the knight. Black must block the check.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 Bc4 Nxe4 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qh5 g6 Qd5
explanation.title: Alekhine Krejcik: 5. Qd5+ against ...g6

explanations.explanation: White checks the king and attacks the knight, seeking to recover material.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 b5 Bxb5 c5 dxc5
explanation.title: Alekhine O’Sullivan: 5. dxc5

explanations.explanation: White captures the c-pawn, but Black can play ...Qa5+, checking the king and attacking the bishop on b5.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 b5 Bxb5 c5 dxc5 Qa5
explanation.title: Alekhine O’Sullivan: 5...Qa5+

explanations.explanation: Black checks the king and attacks the bishop. White must answer both threats.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 Nf3 dxe5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Alekhine Larsen: 5. Nxe5

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the knight, centralizing it and gaining influence over nearby squares.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 exd6
explanation.title: Alekhine Exchange: 5. exd6

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. Black can recapture with either the c-pawn or e-pawn, choosing different pawn structures.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 exd6 cxd6
explanation.title: Alekhine Exchange: 5...cxd6

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on d6 with the c-pawn and can later challenge White’s center with ...Nc6 and ...Bg7.

explanation.moves: e4 Nf6 e5 Nd5 d4 d6 c4 Nb6 f4
explanation.title: Alekhine Defense: Four Pawns Attack

explanations.explanation: White builds a large center with c4, d4, e5 and f4. Black seeks to undermine it from a distance.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 Bc4
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 2. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7. Black must consider Bxf7+ tactics before playing ...b5.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 Bc4 b5
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 2...b5

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop, but White can sacrifice on f7 with check and expose the king.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 Bc4 b5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qh5
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 4. Qh5+

explanations.explanation: White checks the king after sacrificing the bishop. Black must answer the check while guarding against a mating attack.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 c4
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 2. c4

explanations.explanation: White controls d5, gaining space. Black can play ...e5 and enter an open-game structure.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 2. d4

explanations.explanation: White builds a broad center with pawns on d4 and e4. Black can expand with ...b5 or prepare it with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 2...b5

explanations.explanation: Black gains queenside space with ...b5, preparing ...Bb7. White can develop Nf3 or Bd3 to support the center.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 Nf3
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 3. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can fianchetto with ...Bb7 and pressure e4.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 Nf3 Bb7
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 3...Bb7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks e4. White can defend with Bd3 or Nbd2.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 Nf3 Bb7 Bd3
explanation.title: St. George Defense: 4. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops and defends e4. Black can continue development with ...Nf6 or ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 c4
explanation.title: St. George Defense: Three Pawns Attack

explanations.explanation: White gains space and attacks b5, challenging Black’s queenside expansion while building a broad center.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 c4 Bb7
explanation.title: St. George: Three Pawns, 3...Bb7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pressures e4. White can develop Nc3 or Nd2 while accounting for ...bxc4.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 c4 Bb7 Nc3
explanation.title: St. George: Three Pawns, 4. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and defends e4. Black can attack the knight with ...b4.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 c4 Bb7 Nc3 b4
explanation.title: St. George: Three Pawns, 4...b4

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the knight. White can move the knight or play Qb3, attacking b7.

explanation.moves: e4 a6 d4 b5 c4 Bb7 Nc3 b4 Qb3
explanation.title: St. George: Three Pawns, 5. Qb3

explanations.explanation: White moves the queen, countering the attack on the c3 knight. If Black captures the knight with the b-pawn, Qxb7 can win the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 b5 Bxb5
explanation.title: Polish Defense: 2. Bxb5

explanations.explanation: White captures the b-pawn while developing the bishop. Black can play ...Bb7 and pressure the center.

explanation.moves: e4 b5 Bxb5 Bb7 Nc3
explanation.title: Polish Defense: 3. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and defends e4, keeping the extra pawn while Black continues development.

explanation.moves: e4 b5 Bxb5 Bb7 Nc3 f5
explanation.title: Polish Defense: 3...f5

explanations.explanation: Black offers the f-pawn to deflect White’s e-pawn and open the bishop’s long diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4
explanation.title: Owen Defense: 2. d4

explanations.explanation: White builds a center with d4 and e4. Black can fianchetto the bishop with ...Bb7.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Ba6
explanation.title: Owen Defense: Guatemala Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, offering an exchange with White’s f1 bishop. The move leaves queenside light squares less secure.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7
explanation.title: Owen Defense: 2...Bb7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks e4. White can defend with Bd3 or Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3
explanation.title: Owen Defense: 3. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and defends e4. Black can add pressure with ...Nf6 or prepare ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 Nf6
explanation.title: Owen Defense: 3...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and adds pressure on e4. White can add another defender with Qe2 or Nd2.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 f5
explanation.title: Owen Defense: Matovinsky Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black offers the f-pawn to divert White’s e-pawn from the long diagonal, hoping to attack g2 with the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 f5 exf5
explanation.title: Matovinsky Gambit Accepted

explanations.explanation: White captures the f-pawn, opening Black’s bishop’s diagonal toward g2. Black can capture g2 and attack the rook.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 f5 exf5 Bxg2
explanation.title: Matovinsky Gambit: 4...Bxg2

explanations.explanation: Black’s bishop captures on g2 and attacks the rook. White can check with Qh5+ to create counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 f5 exf5 Bxg2 Qh5
explanation.title: Matovinsky Gambit: 5. Qh5+

explanations.explanation: White checks the king along the diagonal. Black must block the check with ...g6.

explanation.moves: e4 b6 d4 Bb7 Bd3 f5 exf5 Bxg2 Qh5 g6
explanation.title: Matovinsky Gambit: 5...g6

explanations.explanation: Black blocks the check with the g-pawn. White can capture on g6 and continue the attack.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bg5 Bg7
explanation.title: Pirc Defense: 4...Bg7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop on the long diagonal. White can develop the queen or choose another setup.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bg5 Bg7 e5
explanation.title: Pirc Defense: 5. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. Black must meet the central threat accurately.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7
explanation.title: Pirc Austrian Attack: 4...Bg7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, aiming at White’s center. White retains a broad pawn formation and can continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3
explanation.title: Pirc Austrian Attack: 5. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops and supports e5, preparing a central advance. Black can castle or challenge the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 O-O
explanation.title: Pirc Austrian Attack: 5...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles, placing the king on g8. White can advance e5 or continue developing pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 d6 d4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4 Bg7 Nf3 c5
explanation.title: Pirc Austrian Attack: 5...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4 before White advances the center. White can exchange on c5 or maintain tension.

explanation.moves: e4 g6 d4 Nf6 e5 Nh5 Be2 d6
explanation.title: Modern Defense: Norwegian Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black plays ...d6, attacking e5, while allowing White to capture the knight on h5. Black seeks central counterplay for the pawn.

explanation.moves: Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nc6 O-O
explanation.title: King’s Indian Attack: 4. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1. Black can gain additional central space with ...e5.

explanation.moves: Nf3 d5 g3 c5 Bg2 Nc6 d4
explanation.title: Réti Opening: Reversed Grünfeld

explanations.explanation: White challenges c5 and confronts Black’s center. Black can exchange on d4.

explanation.moves: c4 e5 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e4 Ng5 c6
explanation.title: English Opening: Adhiban Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black advances the c-pawn, supporting a central plan while offering material for activity.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 exd6 Bxd6 Nf3 g5 h3
explanation.title: From’s Gambit: 5. h3

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn controls g4, but Black can play ...Bg3 mate. The move fails to address the bishop’s threat.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 g4
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 2. g4

explanations.explanation: White advances the g-pawn, exposing the h4–e1 diagonal. Black can deliver mate immediately with ...Qh4.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 g4 Qh4
explanation.title: Bird Opening: Fool’s Mate

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen checks the king; White has no legal reply. The early f- and g-pawn advances opened the mating diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5
explanation.title: Sicilian: Sveshnikov Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. Black gains central space while accepting a potential weakness on d6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Ndb5
explanation.title: Sveshnikov Sicilian: 6. Ndb5

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight and threatens Nd6+, exploiting Black’s weakened d6 square.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5 Nb5
explanation.title: Sicilian: Kalashnikov, 5. Nb5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight threatens Nd6+. Black often plays ...d6 to defend the square.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 e5 Nb5 d6
explanation.title: Kalashnikov Sicilian: 5...d6

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5 and makes Nd6+ harder to achieve. White can continue developing while assessing the knight on b5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 Nc3
explanation.title: Accelerated Dragon: 5. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight rather than playing c4. Black can complete the fianchetto with ...Bg7.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 g6 c4 Bg7
explanation.title: Accelerated Dragon: 5...Bg7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, attacking the d4 knight along the long diagonal. White can defend it with Be3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6
explanation.title: Classical Sicilian

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight alongside the knight on f6 and pawn on d6. The d6 pawn controls e5 and limits an immediate e5 advance.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bc4
explanation.title: Classical Sicilian: Sozin Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7. Black can play ...e6, blunting that diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bg5
explanation.title: Classical Sicilian: Richter-Rauzer

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and attacks the knight, influencing Black’s plans for ...e5 or ...g6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Rg1
explanation.title: Najdorf Sicilian: Freak Attack

explanations.explanation: White moves the rook to prepare a quick g4 advance, seeking kingside attacking chances.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 5...e5

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. White can check with Bb5+ before moving the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Scheveningen Variation

explanations.explanation: Black builds a compact center with pawns on d6 and e6, controlling central squares while keeping pawn breaks available.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Bc4
explanation.title: Scheveningen Sicilian: Sozin Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and aims for active kingside play. Black’s e6 pawn currently blocks the diagonal toward f7.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 Be3
explanation.title: Scheveningen Sicilian: English Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and can prepare f3, g4 and queenside castling for a kingside attack.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 g4
explanation.title: Scheveningen Sicilian: Keres Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances the g-pawn, immediately challenging Black’s kingside and preparing to attack the f6 knight with g5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Dragon Variation

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...Bg7, developing the bishop toward the center while creating kingside targets.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bc4
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 6. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and contests d5, seeking pressure against Black’s kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 6. Be3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and can prepare queenside castling and a Yugoslav Attack. Black normally completes the fianchetto.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 f4
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Levenfish Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the f-pawn, preparing e5 and gaining central space. Black must consider the threatened advance.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5
explanation.title: Sicilian Taimanov: Szén Variation

explanations.explanation: White’s knight eyes d6, exploiting the dark-square weakness created by ...e6. Black can play ...d6 to reinforce the square.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6
explanation.title: Taimanov: 5...d6 against Nb5

explanations.explanation: Black advances the d-pawn, preventing the knight’s entry on d6. White can play c4 or develop Bf4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4
explanation.title: Taimanov: 6. c4

explanations.explanation: White’s c-pawn and e-pawn control d5, establishing a Maróczy bind.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Nf6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Four Knights Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops and pressures e4. Black can later pin the c3 knight with ...Bb4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nc3 Qc7
explanation.title: Sicilian Taimanov: Bastrikov Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen, supporting central and queenside play. White can develop Be3 and defend the d4 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 5. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, preparing Bc4 and castling. Black can open a bishop diagonal with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 5...d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn controls e5 and opens a diagonal for the c8 bishop. White can continue with Bc4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 d6 Bc4
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 6. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7. Black can blunt the diagonal with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 e6
explanation.title: Smith-Morra Gambit: 5...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens the f8 bishop’s diagonal and can blunt White’s bishop pressure on f7. White can continue Bc4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 d4 cxd4 c3 dxc3 Nxc3 Nc6 Nf3 g6
explanation.title: Smith-Morra: Fianchetto Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares ...Bg7, adopting a Dragon-like setup. White can develop Bc4 and continue rapid development.

explanation.moves: Nc3 d5 e4
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 2. e4 against ...d5

explanations.explanation: White builds a central pawn presence with e4. Black can advance ...d4, attacking the c3 knight and gaining space.

explanation.moves: Nc3 f5
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: 1...f5

explanations.explanation: Black controls e4 in Dutch Defense fashion. Black can develop ...Nf6 or choose a Stonewall or fianchetto setup.

explanation.moves: c3 c5
explanation.title: Saragossa Opening: 1...c5

explanations.explanation: Black controls d4. White can play e4, transposing into an Alapin Sicilian, or pursue an independent setup with d4.

explanation.moves: d3 d5 Nc3
explanation.title: Mieses Opening: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, but Black can advance ...d4, attacking it and gaining space.

explanation.moves: e3 d5
explanation.title: Van ’t Kruijs Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black claims central space and controls e4. White can choose a queen’s-pawn setup with d4.

explanation.moves: e3 d5 Nc3
explanation.title: Van ’t Kruijs Opening: 2. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and pressures d5, keeping pawn and piece development flexible.

explanation.moves: e3 d5 Nf3
explanation.title: Van ’t Kruijs Opening: 2. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and controls e5. Black can develop ...Nf6 and defend d5.

explanation.moves: e3 e5 e4
explanation.title: Van ’t Kruijs Opening: Reversed Open Game

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, reaching the pawn layout of 1. e4 e5 with Black to move. The extra e-pawn move has passed the tempo to Black.

explanation.moves: g3 b6 Bg2
explanation.title: Hungarian Opening: 2. Bg2 against ...b6

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop on the long diagonal. Black can contest the center or develop the queenside bishop.

explanation.moves: g3 e5 Bg2
explanation.title: Hungarian Opening: 2. Bg2 against ...e5

explanations.explanation: White completes the fianchetto with the bishop, influencing the center from a distance. Black can continue development.

explanation.moves: g3 h5 Nf3 h4
explanation.title: Hungarian Opening: Van Kuijk Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black advances the h-pawn, offering it to open the h-file. White can capture it or continue developing.

explanation.moves: g4 b5
explanation.title: Grob Opening: 1...b5

explanations.explanation: Black advances the b-pawn, gaining queenside space. White can develop Bg2 while Black prepares to contest the center.

explanation.moves: g4 e5 f3 Qh4
explanation.title: Grob Opening: Fool’s Mate

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen checks the king; White has no legal reply. The g4 and f3 advances opened the mating diagonal.

explanation.moves: c4 c5 Nc3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7 Nf3 e5
explanation.title: Symmetrical English: Wedberg Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn, gaining central space and planning to develop the g8 knight to e7.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 Bf4 e6 e3 d5 Nd2 c5 c3 Nc6 Ngf3
explanation.title: London System: 6. Ngf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the kingside knight behind the c3–d4–e3 pawn structure. Black maintains pressure on d4.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4 Nbd2
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: 6. Nbd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, allowing Black to recover the e5 pawn while preserving a sound structure and the possibility of the bishop pair.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 Bf4 Nc6 Nf3 Bb4 Nc3
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: 6. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, offering it to Black’s bishop. Black can exchange on c3 and continue pressure on e5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bg5 h6 Bh4 c5 d5
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian Leningrad: 6. d5

explanations.explanation: White advances the d-pawn, gaining space. A later e4 can strengthen the center, while Black may challenge it with ...exd5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Qc2 d5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3
explanation.title: Nimzo-Indian: 6. bxc3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on c3, gaining the bishop pair but accepting doubled c-pawns. Both sides have positional chances.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2
explanation.title: King’s Indian: Orthodox, 6. Be2

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and prepares to castle behind a broad center. Black can begin counterplay with ...e5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 Nf3 O-O Be2 e5
explanation.title: King’s Indian: Orthodox, 6...e5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4 and gains space. White can castle before deciding how to resolve the center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3 O-O Be3
explanation.title: King’s Indian Sämisch: 6. Be3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and defends d4. Black can strike in the center with ...e5 or ...c5.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3 O-O Be3 c5
explanation.title: King’s Indian: Sämisch Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4, offering the c-pawn to open lines against White’s center.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 e4 d6 f3 O-O Be3 e5
explanation.title: King’s Indian Sämisch: 6...e5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4, beginning a central challenge. White can advance, exchange or maintain the tension.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Bc4
explanation.title: Grünfeld Exchange: 7. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop actively. Black can pressure the d4 pawn, including with a later ...Bg4 against Nf3.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3
explanation.title: Grünfeld Exchange: 7. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to support the center. White must choose how to develop the remaining bishop and meet pressure on d4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bh4 dxc4 e4
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: 7. e4

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, claiming central space and opening the bishop’s line to c4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: 6. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and supports c4. Black can capture there to enter the Meran Variation.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Meran: 7. Bxc4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on c4 while developing. Black can advance ...b5, gaining time on the bishop and preparing ...Bb7.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Qc2 Bd6
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: Anti-Meran, 6...Bd6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and prepares to castle. Both sides retain central tension.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 dxc4 e3 b5 Nxb5 cxb5 Qf3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 6. Qf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen after sacrificing a knight on b5, seeking tactical compensation against Black’s queenside and king.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 6. Ne5

explanations.explanation: White centralizes the knight and prepares to recover c4, keeping the c1 bishop’s diagonal open.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 e6
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Wiesbaden Variation

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop, preparing ...Bb4. White must consider the c4 pawn and central play.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 e6 f3
explanation.title: Slav Wiesbaden: 7. f3

explanations.explanation: White prepares e4 rather than immediately recovering c4, aiming to attack Black’s bishop on f5 with tempo.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Nh4
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Bled Attack

explanations.explanation: White’s knight attacks the bishop. Black can play ...e6 and recapture with the e-pawn if White exchanges.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Dutch Variation

explanations.explanation: White opens the bishop’s line toward c4 to recover the pawn. The e3 pawn temporarily restricts the c1 bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 Na6
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 6...Na6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, aiming for b4. White can recover c4 and continue development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 7. Bxc4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures the pawn while developing. Black can pin the c3 knight with ...Bb4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 6. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1. Black often plays ...a6, preparing ...b5 to gain time on the c4 bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 Nf3 Nf6 e3 e6 Bxc4 c5 O-O a6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 6...a6

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn supports b5, preparing a queenside advance and bishop development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 dxc4 e4 b5 a4 c6 axb5 cxb5 Nc3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Accepted: 6. Nc3

explanations.explanation: White develops and attacks b5. Black’s a-pawn is constrained by the rook on a1 along the a-file.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 Nbd7
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, reinforcing the center and entering a well-studied classical setup.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Blackburne Variation

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 after developing the bishop to f4. Black can challenge the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3 c5
explanation.title: Blackburne Variation: 6...c5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks d4, striking the center while White’s bishop is on f4 rather than pinning the f6 knight.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3 c5 dxc5
explanation.title: Blackburne Variation: 7. dxc5

explanations.explanation: White captures the c-pawn. Black can recover with the e7 bishop, developing it again.

explanation.moves: d4 e5 Nf3 e4 Ne5
explanation.title: Englund Gambit Declined: 3. Ne5

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight into the center. Black can challenge it with pawn moves and continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 Nd6 Bxc6 dxc6 dxe5 Nf5 Qxd8 Kxd8
explanation.title: Berlin Defense: Berlin Wall Endgame

explanations.explanation: After the queen exchange, Black’s king cannot castle. Black has the bishop pair, while White has a pawn majority on the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 7. Bb3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop from the b-pawn’s attack, preserving it on the a2–g8 diagonal. Black can continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 7...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles, placing the king on g8. White can play c3 to prepare d4 or choose an anti-Marshall setup.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O a4
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: Anti-Marshall, 8. a4

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn attacks b5. After axb5, Black’s a-pawn can become pinned to the rook on a8 along the a-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 8. c3

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4. Black can challenge immediately with the Marshall Gambit, ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks e4 and offers the d-pawn for rapid piece activity. White can accept with exd5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 11. Rxe5

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on e5 with the rook. Black must address the pressure on the knight on d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 11...c6

explanations.explanation: Black supports the d5 knight. An exchange on d5 would leave Black with active bishops and queenside pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6 d4 Bd6
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 12...Bd6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks the rook. White must move it, commonly back to e1.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 Nxd5 Nxe5 Nxe5 Rxe5 c6 d4 Bd6 Re1 Qh4 g3 Qh3
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 14...Qh3

explanations.explanation: Black positions the queen near White’s king. Black may develop ...Bg4, creating threats involving the bishop and queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5 e4
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: Steiner Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. White can capture the c6 knight with dxc6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 7...d6

explanations.explanation: Black supports e5. White usually prepares d4 with c3 before opening the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 8. c3 after ...d6

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4, aiming for a central break. Black can castle or consider ...Na5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 8...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles, placing the king on g8. White can play d4 or continue preparing the central break.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: 9. h3

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn controls g4, limiting ...Bg4. Black has several plans for queenside development.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Bb7
explanation.title: Closed Ruy Lopez: Flohr System

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop toward the long diagonal and can add pressure to e4 with ...Re8. The c6 knight currently blocks the bishop’s diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Bb7 d4 Re8 a4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Zaitsev, 11. a4

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn attacks b5, probing Black’s queenside structure. Black can consider ...h6 to limit Ng5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 c3 O-O h3 Na5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Chigorin Defense

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the bishop and clears c6 for the c-pawn. White commonly retreats the bishop to c2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 d6 d4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Rosen Attack

explanations.explanation: White challenges e5, but Black can exploit tactical pressure on d4 with ...Nxd4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 b5 Bb3
explanation.title: Open Ruy Lopez: 7. Bb3

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and keeps castling available. Black may later challenge the e5 knight with ...Bd6.
