explanation.title: Najdorf: Poisoned Pawn Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks b2. White can defend it or allow the capture in pursuit of development.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2
explanation.title: Poisoned Pawn: 8. Qd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen, allowing ...Qxb2 while preparing to castle queenside and seek compensation.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2
explanation.title: Poisoned Pawn Accepted

explanations.explanation: Black captures the b-pawn. White can attack the queen with Rb1 and develop with tempo.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2 Rb1
explanation.title: Poisoned Pawn: 9. Rb1

explanations.explanation: White’s rook attacks the queen along the b-file. Black must move the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 Qb6 Qd2 Qxb2 Rb1 Qa3
explanation.title: Poisoned Pawn: 9...Qa3

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the queen from the rook’s attack. White can develop while seeking compensation for the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5
explanation.title: Najdorf: Polugaevsky Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the b-pawn for queenside counterplay. White can advance e5, attacking the f6 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 8. e5

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the knight. Black can respond with ...dxe5, creating tactical play.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 8...dxe5

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn. White can recapture with fxe5, continuing the attack on f6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 9. fxe5

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on e5 and attacks the knight on f6. Black can develop the queen to c7 and seek tactical counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 9...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen, creating tactical counterplay despite the threat to f6. White can capture the knight and enter a forcing line.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 10. exf6

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight. Black can check with ...Qe5+, exposing a tactical idea against the bishop on g5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 10...Qe5+

explanations.explanation: Black checks the king and attacks the bishop on g5. White must block the check while accounting for the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e6 g4 h6
explanation.title: Scheveningen: Keres, 6...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn controls g5, preventing White from immediately advancing the g-pawn there.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Bc4 Bg7
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 6...Bg7 after Bc4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop on the long diagonal and prepares to castle. White can continue development toward a kingside attack.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 6...Bg7 after Be3

explanations.explanation: Black completes the fianchetto with the bishop. White can play f3 to control g4 and prepare queenside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav Attack

explanations.explanation: White supports e4 and controls g4, preparing Qd2 and queenside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 10. Kh1

explanations.explanation: White moves the king out of the bishop’s check. Black must address the threats to the queen and e4 knight while pursuing the attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1 Qh4 Rxe4 dxe4 Qd8 Qxd8
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 12...Qxd8

explanations.explanation: Black captures the queen. White can recapture with the knight, completing the queen exchange with check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1 Qh4 Rxe4 dxe4 Qd8 Qxd8 Nxd8
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 13. Nxd8+

explanations.explanation: White recaptures the queen on d8 with check. Black can capture the knight with the king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1 Qh4 Rxe4 dxe4 Qd8 Qxd8 Nxd8 Kxd8
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 13...Kxd8

explanations.explanation: Black captures the knight. White can capture the bishop on h2 with the king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1 Qh4 Rxe4 dxe4 Qd8 Qxd8 Nxd8 Kxd8 Kxh2
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 14. Kxh2

explanations.explanation: White captures the bishop. After the forcing sequence, White has two minor pieces for Black’s rook and pawns.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Nxe4 d4 exd4 Re1 d5 Nxd4 Bd6 Nxc6 Bxh2 Kh1 Qh4 Rxe4 dxe4 Qd8 Qxd8 Nxd8 Kxd8 Kxh2 Be6
explanation.title: Riga Variation: 14...Be6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, contesting White’s light-squared bishop. Both sides can now choose among several continuations.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 d6 h3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Modern Steinitz, 5. h3

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn controls g4, discouraging ...Bg4 while Black chooses a development plan.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qd5 c4 Qd6 Nxa7 Bd7 Bxd7 Qxd7 Qh5 g6 Qe5 Kf7
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 12...Kf7

explanations.explanation: Black moves the king out of check. White must consider whether the queen could escape after capturing the rook on h8.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qd5 c4 Qd6 Nxa7 Bd7 Bxd7 Qxd7 Qh5 g6 Qe5 Kf7 Nb5
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 13. Nb5

explanations.explanation: White’s knight attacks c7, while the queen also pressures e4. Black can answer with ...c6, attacking the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qd5 c4 Qd6 Nxa7 Bd7 Bxd7 Qxd7 Qh5 g6 Qe5 Kf7 Nb5 c6
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 13...c6

explanations.explanation: Black’s c-pawn attacks the knight. White can retreat or offer a queen exchange with Qd4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qd5 c4 Qd6 Nxa7 Bd7 Bxd7 Qxd7 Qh5 g6 Qe5 Kf7 Nb5 c6 Qd4
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 14. Qd4

explanations.explanation: White’s queen attacks the black queen. Black can exchange or move a rook to d8, keeping the knight on b5 under pressure.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qg5 Qe2 Nf6 Nxa7 Kd8 Nxc8 Qxg2
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 10...Qxg2

explanations.explanation: Black captures on g2 and attacks the rook. White must defend or move the rook while the knight on c8 is exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qg5 Qe2 Nf6 f4 Qxf4 Ne5 c6 d4 Qh4 g3 Qh3
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 12...Qh3

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the queen and the bishop on b5 must address Black’s c6 pawn. White can develop Bc4 with pressure on f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 f5 Nc3 fxe4 Nxe4 d5 Nxe5 dxe4 Nxc6 Qg5 Qe2 Nf6 f4 Qxf4 Ne5 c6 d4 Qh4 g3 Qh3 Bc4 Be6
explanation.title: Schliemann Defense: 13...Be6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop to oppose White’s active pieces. White can decide how to develop the remaining minor piece.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 b4 Be7
explanation.title: Italian Game: Dubov, 6...Be7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop from the b-pawn’s attack. It controls g5 and helps shield the king along the e-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5
explanation.title: Italian Game: Rybasov, 7. Bxd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn with the bishop, interrupting Black’s central threat. Black can develop ...Nf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bg5 O-O Ne5
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 9. Ne5+

explanations.explanation: White retreats the knight to e5 with check. Black must answer the check while the bishop on d5 remains exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bg5 O-O Ne5 Be6
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 9...Be6

explanations.explanation: Black blocks the check with the bishop. White must consider Black’s tactical threats before exchanging it.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bg5 O-O Ne5 Be6 c3
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 10. c3

explanations.explanation: White’s c-pawn attacks the knight. Black can retreat to c6 while maintaining activity.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Bg5 O-O Ne5 Be6 c3 Nc6
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 10...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the knight from the pawn’s attack. White must continue to address the tactical pressure on the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Nxh8
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 8. Nxh8

explanations.explanation: White captures the rook with the knight. Black has active pieces and open lines with which to attack White’s undeveloped position.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Nxh8 Bg4
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 8...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks the queen. White must respond while Black threatens the bishop on d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 d4 Nxd4 Nxe5 Qe7 Nxf7 d5 Bxd5 Nf6 Nxh8 Bg4 Bf7
explanation.title: Rybasov Gambit: 9. Bf7+

explanations.explanation: White moves the bishop to f7 with check, saving it from attack. Black must answer the check.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nd4 Nxe5 Qg5 Nxf7 Qxg2 Rf1 Qxe4
explanation.title: Blackburne Shilling: 6...Qxe4+

explanations.explanation: Black captures the e-pawn with check, continuing the attack against White’s king. White must answer the check carefully.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 6...Rf8

explanations.explanation: Black moves the rook to the open f-file, supporting threats against f2 and White’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7. Bxc6

explanations.explanation: White captures the knight, reducing Black’s attacking resources. Black can recapture with the d-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6 dxc6
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7...dxc6

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on c6 with the d-pawn, opening the d-file for the queen and retaining active piece play.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6 dxc6 d3
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8. d3

explanations.explanation: White’s d-pawn supports e4 and opens the c1 bishop’s diagonal. Black can add pressure with ...Ng4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6 dxc6 d3 Ng4
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8...Ng4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and attacks f2, adding to the pressure along the f-file and bishop diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6 dxc6 d3 Ng4 Nh3
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 9. Nh3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the knight to h3, defending f2 and clearing g5 for the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 Bxc6 dxc6 d3 Ng4 Nh3 Nxf2
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 9...Nxf2

explanations.explanation: Black captures the f-pawn with the knight. The position remains tactical, with both kings exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 O-O
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1 and defending f2 with the rook. Black can continue the attack with developed pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 O-O d6
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7...d6

explanations.explanation: Black’s d-pawn supports e5 and opens the c8 bishop’s diagonal. It also affects how Black can recapture on c6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 O-O d6 c3
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8. c3

explanations.explanation: White prepares d4 and opens a diagonal for the queen toward a4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Bxf7 Ke7 Bd5 Rf8 O-O d6 c3 Bg4
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and attacks the queen. White must move or otherwise defend the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 6...Qe7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen and prepares further threats. White can complete the knight fork by capturing the rook on h8.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7 Nxh8
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7. Nxh8

explanations.explanation: White captures the rook with the knight. Black can strike in the center with ...d5 while White’s king is exposed.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7 Nxh8 d5
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 7...d5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges e4 and opens central lines. White can capture on d5 or take the bishop on f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7 Nxh8 d5 Kxf2
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8. Kxf2

explanations.explanation: White captures the bishop with the king. Black can recapture material with ...dxc4 and maintain central play.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7 Nxh8 d5 exd5
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8. exd5

explanations.explanation: White captures the d-pawn. Black retains active pieces and can continue attacking the exposed king.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 Bc5 Nxf7 Bxf2 Kf1 Qe7 Nxh8 d5 exd5 Nd4
explanation.title: Traxler Counterattack: 8...Nd4

explanations.explanation: Black centralizes the knight, preparing threats including ...Bg4 against White’s queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Ng5 exd3 Bxd3 h6 Nxf7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Dinic: 6. Nxf7

explanations.explanation: White captures on f7, forking Black’s queen and rook. Black can limit the damage by capturing the bishop with the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Bd3 dxe4 Bxe4 Nf6 Bf3 Bf5 g4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Mieses: Hibbins-Khan Variation

explanations.explanation: White’s g-pawn attacks the bishop and gains kingside space. Black must respond to the threat.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 Nf3 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 6...Nd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, supporting e5 and preparing further development. White can advance h4 against the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 6...Nd7 after h4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight while the bishop on g6 faces pressure from White’s h-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 7. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight and can consider Ne5. Black often develops ...Nd7 to contest that square.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 7...Nd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, contesting e5. White can play h5 to attack the bishop and gain kingside space.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 8. h5

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn attacks the bishop. Black must move it to safety.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 8...Bh7

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop from the h-pawn’s attack. White can develop Bd3 and offer an exchange.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 9. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and offers an exchange with the h7 bishop. Black can capture on d3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 9...Bxd3

explanations.explanation: Black captures the bishop. White can recapture with the queen, preserving the pawn structure.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 10. Qxd3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the queen. Black can continue development with ...Ngf6, ...e6 or ...Qc7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 Qc7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 10...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen, preparing possible queenside castling and controlling f4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 10...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens a diagonal for the f8 bishop. White can develop Bf4 or Bd2 and choose a castling plan.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 11. Bd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and prepares queenside castling. The advanced h-pawn can support kingside play.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2 Ngf6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 11...Ngf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, keeping both castling options available. White can castle queenside.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2 Ngf6 O-O-O
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 12. O-O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles queenside, placing the king on c1 and bringing the rook toward the center. Black can prepare to castle.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2 Ngf6 O-O-O Be7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 12...Be7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, preparing kingside castling. White can improve king safety with Kb1 or continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bd2 Qc7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 11...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen, keeping queenside castling available. White can decide how to deploy the remaining knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bf4 Qa5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 11...Qa5+

explanations.explanation: Black checks the king with the queen, encouraging a response that may affect White’s queenside castling plans.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 7...e6

explanations.explanation: Black opens the bishop’s diagonal but permits White’s knight to enter e5. White can play Ne5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 h5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Classical: 7. h5

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn attacks the bishop again. Black can retreat it to h7; White may continue kingside play.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 Bg6 N1f3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: 6. N1f3

explanations.explanation: White develops the second knight, preparing counterplay while the knight on g5 pressures Black’s kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 Bg6 N1f3 h6 Ne6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Martian Gambit

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight into Black’s position and offers it for an attack. Black can accept with ...fxe6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 Bg6 N1f3 h6 Ne6 fxe6 Ne5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Martian: 8. Ne5

explanations.explanation: White centralizes the knight after sacrificing the other knight. The piece controls squares near Black’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Ng5 h6 Nxf7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Alien Gambit

explanations.explanation: White sacrifices the knight on f7, seeking to draw Black’s king into the open and generate an attack.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Be3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 6. Be3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, preparing a solid central setup and kingside play. Black can develop ...Nd7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Van der Wiel: 6. Nge2

explanations.explanation: White develops the kingside knight, threatening Nf4 and h4 against Black’s bishop. Black can counter in the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Van der Wiel: 7. h4

explanations.explanation: White’s h-pawn supports g5 and prepares h5 against the g6 bishop. Black can challenge the pawn chain with ...h5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Van der Wiel: 7...h5

explanations.explanation: Black attacks g4, challenging White’s kingside pawn advance. White can continue to pressure the bishop with Nf4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4 Bh7 Nxh5 Nc6 dxc5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Van der Wiel: 10. dxc5

explanations.explanation: White captures the c-pawn. Black can recapture with the bishop and seek counterplay against e5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4 Bh7 Nxh5 Nc6 dxc5 Bxc5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Van der Wiel: 10...Bxc5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on c5 with the bishop, developing it and creating threats against White’s center.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Bb4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 5...Bb4+

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop with check. White must block the check and can choose how to continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nd7 O-O Ne7 Nh4 Bg6 Nd2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 8. Nd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, keeping c3 available to support d4 and allowing a later Nf3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nd7 O-O Ne7 Nh4 Bg6 Nd2 c5 c3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 9. c3

explanations.explanation: White supports d4. Black can continue development with ...Nc6 and pressure the knight on h4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nf3 e6 Be2 Nd7 O-O Ne7 Nh4 Bg6 Nd2 c5 c3 Nc6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: 9...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and adds pressure on d4. White can exchange the h4 knight for the bishop on g6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls: 6. cxd4

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on d4 with the c-pawn. Black can develop ...Bg4 and challenge the knight defending d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls: 6...Bg4

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop and pins the knight to the queen, increasing pressure on d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4 Bb5
explanation.title: Botvinnik-Carls: 7. Bb5

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and pins the c6 knight to the king. Black can continue with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 dxe4 f3
explanation.title: French Winawer: Winckelmann-Reimer Gambit

explanations.explanation: White’s f-pawn attacks e4, offering an exchange to open lines. Black can instead challenge White’s center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Ba5 b4
explanation.title: French Winawer: 6. b4

explanations.explanation: White’s b-pawn attacks the bishop, breaking the pin on c3. Black must choose how to respond.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Ba5 b4 cxd4
explanation.title: French Winawer: Armenian Line

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn, leaving both the c3 knight and a5 bishop exposed. White can play Nb5 and create threats.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3
explanation.title: French Winawer: 6. bxc3

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on c3, accepting doubled c-pawns and gaining the bishop pair. White can seek kingside counterplay with Qg4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7
explanation.title: French Winawer: 6...Ne7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, keeping f6 available and preparing kingside development. White can develop or attack g7 with Qg4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Nf3
explanation.title: French Winawer: 7. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, choosing a positional setup. Black can develop the c8 bishop or continue kingside development.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4
explanation.title: French Winawer: 7. Qg4

explanations.explanation: White’s queen attacks g7. Black must decide whether to defend the pawn or seek counterplay elsewhere.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Kf8
explanation.title: French Winawer: Eingorn Variation

explanations.explanation: Black moves the king to defend g7, giving up castling rights. White can develop Nf3 and continue pressuring the kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O
explanation.title: French Winawer: Warsaw Variation

explanations.explanation: Black castles, placing the king on g8 despite White’s queen’s pressure on the kingside. White can continue development.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O Nf3
explanation.title: French Winawer: 8. Nf3 after castling

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight, bringing another piece toward Black’s king. Black can develop the queenside knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O Nf3 Nbc6
explanation.title: French Winawer: 8...Nbc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queenside knight, increasing pressure on White’s center. White can develop the f1 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O Nf3 Nbc6 Bd3
explanation.title: French Winawer: 9. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, aiming toward h7. Black must consider kingside tactics while maintaining pressure on the center.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O Nf3 Nbc6 Bd3 f5
explanation.title: French Winawer: 9...f5

explanations.explanation: Black advances the f-pawn, blocking the bishop’s diagonal toward h7. White can capture en passant with exf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 O-O Nf3 Nbc6 Bd3 f5 exf6
explanation.title: French Winawer: 10. exf6 en passant

explanations.explanation: White captures on f6 en passant, reopening attacking lines and attacking the knight. Black can recapture with the rook.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7
explanation.title: French Winawer: Poisoned Pawn Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen, allowing Qxg7 while seeking counterplay against White’s queenside and center.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7 Bd3
explanation.title: French Winawer: Poisoned Pawn Declined

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop rather than immediately capturing g7, preparing kingside castling and a less forcing game.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7 Qxg7 Rg8
explanation.title: Winawer Poisoned Pawn: 8...Rg8

explanations.explanation: Black moves the rook to g8, attacking White’s queen on g7. White can capture h7 while moving the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7 Qxg7 Rg8 Qxh7
explanation.title: Winawer Poisoned Pawn: 9. Qxh7

explanations.explanation: White captures the h-pawn and moves the queen out of the rook’s attack. Black seeks active counterplay against White’s center.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7 Qxg7 Rg8 Qxh7 cxd4
explanation.title: Winawer Poisoned Pawn: 9...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn, opening the c-file and removing a defender of e5. White must calculate before recapturing.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Qa5
explanation.title: French Winawer: Portisch-Hook Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s queen attacks c3. White can defend the pawn with Bd2 while Black seeks queenside counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Qc7
explanation.title: French Winawer: 6...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen toward a c-file that may open after ...cxd4. White can develop Qg4 and attack g7.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5 Nfd7 Bxe7 Qxe7
explanation.title: French Classical: 6...Qxe7

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures the bishop with the queen. White can pursue the main central plan with f4 or choose another setup.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5 c3
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 6. c3

explanations.explanation: White reinforces d4, the base of the pawn chain. Black can add pressure with ...Nc6 and ...Qb6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 6...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and adds pressure on d4. White must decide how to defend the pawn if Black brings the queen to b6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Ne2
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: 7. Ne2

explanations.explanation: White develops and defends d4, keeping f3 available for the d2 knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nd2 Nf6 e5 Nfd7 Bd3 c5 c3 Nc6 Ngf3
explanation.title: French Tarrasch: Korchnoi Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight to defend d4, leaving the other knight less direct access to f3. Black can increase pressure with ...Qb6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3
explanation.title: French Advance: Milner-Barry Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, allowing pressure on d4 but relying on tactical counterplay if Black captures the pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4
explanation.title: Milner-Barry Gambit: 6...cxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn. White can recapture with cxd4; Black must calculate carefully before capturing again on d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3
explanation.title: French Advance: 6. a3

explanations.explanation: White’s a-pawn controls b4 and prepares a queenside advance. Black can develop or fix the queenside with ...c4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 Nh6
explanation.title: French Advance: Lputian Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, aiming for f5. White must consider the attack on b2 before exchanging on h6.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 a3 c4
explanation.title: French Advance: 6...c4

explanations.explanation: Black advances the c-pawn, restricting White’s bishop and hindering b4 because an en passant capture could follow.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5 Be2
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 11. Be2

explanations.explanation: White blocks the queen’s check with the bishop. Black can capture the bishop on g5 with ...Qxg5.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5 Be2 Qxg5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 11...Qxg5

explanations.explanation: Black captures the bishop with the queen, recovering material after the forcing central sequence.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5 Be2 Qxg5 O-O
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 12. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1. Black must develop quickly and address White’s active pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5 Be2 Qxg5 O-O Qe5
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 12...Qe5

explanations.explanation: Black places the queen centrally and threatens ...Bc5. White can move the king to h1 to avoid checks.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 Bg5 e6 f4 b5 e5 dxe5 fxe5 Qc7 exf6 Qe5 Be2 Qxg5 O-O Qe5 Kh1
explanation.title: Polugaevsky Variation: 13. Kh1

explanations.explanation: White moves the king away from checks on the g1–a7 diagonal. Black must continue developing.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 Nc6
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Belezky Line

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight instead of castling immediately. White can develop Bc4 and continue the Yugoslav setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 7...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles kingside, placing the king on g8. White often castles queenside, producing opposite-side attacks.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 8. Qd2

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen and prepares queenside castling, while supporting kingside attacking plans.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 8...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can choose a bishop development and prepare queenside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 9. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7 and prepares queenside castling, adding pressure against Black’s king.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 9...Bd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop, clearing c8 for the rook and preparing counterplay on the c-file.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7 O-O-O
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: Yugoslav, 10. O-O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles queenside, placing the king opposite Black’s castled king. Both sides can attack on the flanks.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7 O-O-O Rc8
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 10...Rc8

explanations.explanation: Black moves the rook onto the c-file, aiming through the half-open file toward the bishop on c4 and White’s queenside.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Bg7 f3 O-O Qd2 Nc6 Bc4 Bd7 O-O-O Rc8 Bb3
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 11. Bb3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop from the c8 rook’s line, keeping it aimed toward Black’s kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4
explanation.title: Sicilian Dragon: 6...Ng4

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the bishop, but White can play Bb5+, interrupting the defense of the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6
explanation.title: Taimanov Sicilian: 6...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops and attacks e4. White can defend it with the other knight on c3.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6 N1c3
explanation.title: Taimanov Sicilian: 7. N1c3

explanations.explanation: White develops the b1 knight and defends e4. Black can challenge the b5 knight with ...a6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6 N1c3 a6
explanation.title: Taimanov Sicilian: 7...a6

explanations.explanation: Black’s a-pawn attacks the knight. White can retreat to a3 or d4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6 N1c3 a6 Na3
explanation.title: Taimanov Sicilian: 8. Na3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the knight, where it supports c4. The c4 and e4 pawns restrain Black’s ...d5 break.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 e6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nc6 Nb5 d6 c4 Nf6 N1c3 a6 Na3 d5
explanation.title: Taimanov Sicilian: Garry Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black advances the d-pawn, challenging White’s pawn bind. White can capture and open the center.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Bc4 d6 c3 Nc6
explanation.title: Sicilian: Camelot Defense

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight against White’s Bowdler setup. White can use the opened d1–a4 diagonal and prepare central play.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nf6 dxc5
explanation.title: Sicilian: 4. dxc5 against ...Nf6

explanations.explanation: White captures the c-pawn, opening the d-file toward Black’s queen. Black can counterattack e4 with ...Nxe4.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 e5 Bb5 Nbd7
explanation.title: Open Sicilian: 6...Nbd7

explanations.explanation: Black blocks the bishop’s check by developing the knight. White can continue development while Black prepares a central setup.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: 7...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the bishop. White can retreat to h4, keeping pressure on the knight.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: 8...g5

explanations.explanation: Black’s g-pawn attacks the bishop and blocks its line to f6. White can sacrifice a knight with Nxg5 to continue the attack.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5 Nxg5
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: 9. Nxg5

explanations.explanation: White captures on g5, temporarily sacrificing the knight to reopen the bishop’s diagonal. Black can recapture with ...hxg5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5 Nxg5 hxg5 Bxg5
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: 10. Bxg5

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on g5, restoring pressure on the f6 knight. Black can develop ...Nbd7 to defend it.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5 Nxg5 hxg5 Bxg5 Nbd7
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: 10...Nbd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops and defends the knight on f6. White can choose between several attacking setups.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 dxc4 e4 b5 e5 h6 Bh4 g5 Nxg5 hxg5 Bxg5 Nbd7 g3
explanation.title: Semi-Slav Botvinnik: Lilienthal Variation

explanations.explanation: White prepares Bg2, aiming for the long diagonal. Black can contest it with ...Bb7.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bh4
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: Anti-Moscow Variation

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop, keeping pressure on f6 and offering c4. Black can accept with ...dxc4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bh4 dxc4 e4 g5
explanation.title: Anti-Moscow: 7...g5

explanations.explanation: Black’s g-pawn attacks the bishop. White can retreat to g3 while maintaining a broad center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 Bg5 h6 Bh4 dxc4 e4 g5 Bg3 b5
explanation.title: Anti-Moscow: 8...b5

explanations.explanation: Black defends c4 and gains queenside space. White can develop Be2 and prepare to castle.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: Meran Variation

explanations.explanation: Black captures on c4 with an attack on the d3 bishop. White can recapture with Bxc4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5
explanation.title: Meran Variation: 7...b5

explanations.explanation: Black’s b-pawn attacks the bishop, gaining queenside space and opening b7 for Black’s bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5 Bd3
explanation.title: Meran Variation: 8. Bd3

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop, keeping support for a future e4 advance. Black can reinforce b5 with ...a6.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5 Bd3 a6
explanation.title: Meran Variation: 8...a6

explanations.explanation: Black supports b5, preparing to challenge the center with ...c5. White can advance e4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5 Bd3 a6 e4
explanation.title: Meran Variation: 9. e4

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, gaining space and opening the c1 bishop’s diagonal. Black can challenge it with ...c5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Bd3 dxc4 Bxc4 b5 Bd3 a6 e4 c5
explanation.title: Meran Variation: 9...c5

explanations.explanation: Black challenges d4 and opens the c8 bishop’s diagonal. White must choose how to resolve the center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 e6 e3 Nbd7 Qc2
explanation.title: Semi-Slav: Anti-Meran, 6. Qc2

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen, avoiding an immediate Meran structure and retaining several plans. Black can develop ...Bd6.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Nb6
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 7...Nb6

explanations.explanation: Black’s knight attacks the c4 knight. White can retreat to e5 or exchange.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 7...Qc7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen to prepare ...e5. White can play g3 and develop the bishop to g2.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3
explanation.title: Slav Defense: 8. g3

explanations.explanation: White prepares Bg2 and can also develop the other bishop to f4. Black retains the ...e5 break.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5
explanation.title: Slav Defense: Carlsbad Variation

explanations.explanation: Black advances the e-pawn, opening the f8 bishop’s diagonal and challenging White’s center.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: 9...Nxe5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on e5 with the knight. White can play Bf4, pinning it to the queen on c7.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5 Bf4
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: 10. Bf4

explanations.explanation: White’s bishop pins the knight to the queen. Black can add a defender with ...Nfd7.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5 Bf4 Nfd7
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: 10...Nfd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and defends e5. White can complete the kingside fianchetto.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5 Bf4 Nfd7 Bg2
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: 11. Bg2

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and prepares to castle. Black can defend the e5 knight or challenge White’s bishop with ...g5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5 Bf4 Nfd7 Bg2 g5
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: Morozevich Variation

explanations.explanation: Black’s g-pawn attacks the bishop, gaining time while weakening the kingside.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 Nbd7 Nxc4 Qc7 g3 e5 dxe5 Nxe5 Bf4 Nfd7 Bg2 g5 Ne3
explanation.title: Slav Carlsbad: 12. Ne3

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight, preparing to recapture on f5 if Black takes the bishop on f4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 e6 f3 Bb4
explanation.title: Slav Wiesbaden: 7...Bb4

explanations.explanation: Black pins the c3 knight to the king, exploiting the weakened b4 square. White can still advance e4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 Ne5 e6 f3 Bb4 e4
explanation.title: Slav Wiesbaden: 8. e4

explanations.explanation: White’s e-pawn attacks the bishop and opens the f1 bishop’s line toward c4. Black must respond actively.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 8. O-O

explanations.explanation: White castles, placing the king on g1 and ending the pin on the c3 knight. White can prepare e4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O Nbd7
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 8...Nbd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, contesting e5. White can continue with Qe2 or attack the bishop with Nh4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O Nbd7 Qe2
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 9. Qe2

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen and prepares e4. Black can castle or retreat the bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O Nbd7 Qe2 Bg6 e4
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 10. e4 after ...Bg6

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn, building a broad center. Black can castle or challenge it with pieces.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 8...O-O

explanations.explanation: Black castles, placing the king on g8. Black can consider ...Bg6 before White establishes e4.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O Qe2
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 9. Qe2 after ...O-O

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen and threatens e4 with an attack on the f5 bishop. Black can retreat the bishop or develop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O Qe2 Bg6
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 9...Bg6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop, removing it from the threatened e4 advance. White can choose how to continue development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O Qe2 Nbd7
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 9...Nbd7

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight and prepares ...Nb6. White can advance e4 and attack the bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O Qe2 Nbd7 e4
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 10. e4

explanations.explanation: White advances the e-pawn and attacks the bishop, gaining central space with tempo.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 c6 Nf3 Nf6 Nc3 dxc4 a4 Bf5 e3 e6 Bxc4 Bb4 O-O O-O Qe2 Nbd7 e4 Bg6
explanation.title: Slav Dutch: 10...Bg6

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop, keeping pressure on e4. White can defend the pawn with Bd3.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 6. Nf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can choose a classical ...Nbd7 setup or play ...h6 to question the bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 6...h6

explanations.explanation: Black’s h-pawn attacks the bishop. White can retreat to h4 or choose another response.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 Ne4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Lasker Defense

explanations.explanation: Black centralizes the knight, opening the e7 bishop’s attack on White’s bishop at h4. Exchanges can follow.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e3 O-O Nf3 h6 Bh4 b6
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Tartakower Defense

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to develop the light-squared bishop after ...b6, seeking activity outside the pawn chain.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 Nf6 Nf3 Be7 Bf4 O-O e3 c5 dxc5 Bxc5
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: 7...Bxc5

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on c5 with the bishop. White can exchange on d5 or continue development.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4 dxe4 Nxe4 Bb4 Bd2 Qxd4
explanation.title: Queen’s Gambit Declined: Marshall, 6...Qxd4

explanations.explanation: Black captures the d-pawn with the queen. White can capture the bishop on b4 and obtain active play.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4 dxe4 Nxe4 Bb4 Bd2 Qxd4 Bxb4
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 7. Bxb4

explanations.explanation: White captures the bishop and places the bishop on an active diagonal. Black can recapture the knight with ...Qxe4+.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4 dxe4 Nxe4 Bb4 Bd2 Qxd4 Bxb4 Qxe4
explanation.title: Marshall Gambit: 7...Qxe4+

explanations.explanation: Black captures the knight with check. White must block the check, entering a complex position.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 e5 dxe5 Ng4 e3 Nxe5 Nh3
explanation.title: Budapest Gambit: Shereshevsky Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight toward f4, aiming to restrain ...d5; a queenside fianchetto is another part of the plan.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 Bg7 Nf3 d6
explanation.title: King's Indian Defence: Flexible move order

explanations.explanation: Black has completed the ...d6 setup. White can occupy the center with e4, entering a main King's Indian structure.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Bc4 c5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defence: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: Black challenges White's center with the c-pawn. White can develop the king's knight and castle as the position opens.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defence: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: The c-pawn attacks d4, working with the g7 bishop against White's broad center. White has several ways to support or advance it.

explanation.moves: d4 Nf6 c4 g6 Nc3 d5 cxd5 Nxd5 e4 Nxc3 bxc3 Bg7 Nf3 c5 Bb5
explanation.title: Grünfeld Defence: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: The bishop gives check. Black can develop with ...Nc6, though White may then advance d5 against the knight.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Bc4 Bc5 Nf3
explanation.title: Bishop's Opening: Classical Defence

explanations.explanation: The knight attacks e5, while a later d4 can gain time against Black's c5 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Bc5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defence

explanations.explanation: White takes e5 with a fork idea, but Black has queen moves such as ...Qh4 that create counterplay.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Bc5 Nxe5 Qh4
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Classical Defence

explanations.explanation: Black's queen pressures f2, creating counterplay after White's knight capture on e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Ba4 Nf6 O-O Be7 Re1 b5 Bb3 O-O c3 d5 exd5
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Marshall Gambit

explanations.explanation: White has accepted the central pawn. Black can recapture with ...Nxd5 or try the aggressive ...e4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6 Bxc6 dxc6 O-O Bg4 h3
explanation.title: Ruy Lopez: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White questions the bishop on g4 with h3, but Black can also meet it with the surprising counterthrust ...h5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: Black's knight attacks e4, but White can advance dxe5 and exploit the resulting tactics.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Ng4 Bg5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: The bishop attacks Black's queen. Black can interpose with ...f6, driving the bishop back.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Ng4 Bg5 f6 exf6 gxf6 Bh4
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: The bishop retreats after ...f6 and the exchanges on f6; Black's doubled f-pawns leave the kingside structure damaged.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Nxe4 Qd5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: White's queen attacks the knight and also threatens f7. Black must address both tactical ideas.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 d6 Bg5
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Bishop check on the queen

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop with an attack on the queen; Black can block the diagonal in several ways.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 b4 Bb6
explanation.title: Italian Game: Dubov Gambit

explanations.explanation: The bishop on b6 eyes b4, making an immediate recovery of the d4-pawn awkward. White can instead advance e5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 c3 Nf6 d4 exd4 cxd4 Bb4 Nc3
explanation.title: Italian Game: Greco Gambit

explanations.explanation: White blocks the check with Nc3, offering the e4 pawn in return for a lead in development and active pieces.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's h-pawn controls g4 and can help open the h-file. Castling into the attack needs care.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5 c3
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: The c-pawn supports d4, which would interrupt the c5 bishop's pressure on f2. Black can still try ...Ng4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Be2 h5 c3 Ng4
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's knight and c5 bishop both aim at f2. White can challenge that pressure with d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: The bishop pins the knight to the queen, but Black can sacrifice the queen temporarily with ...Nxe4 and exploit threats against f2.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 Nc6 Nxc6 dxc6 d3 Bc5 Bg5 Nxe4
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Stafford Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black plays ...Nxe4 despite the pin. Capturing the queen allows a dangerous attack beginning with ...Bxf2+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nf6 Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7 d4 c5
explanation.title: Petrov Defence: Cochrane Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black strikes at White's central pawn while avoiding the tactical difficulties of ...Nxe4 followed by Qh5+.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Be7 dxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 dxe5 Qh5
explanation.title: Philidor Defence: Tactical queen sortie

explanations.explanation: The queen attacks f7 and also attacks e5. Black can meet the threat with ...g6, although Qxe5 then wins a pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Ngf6 dxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 dxe5
explanation.title: Philidor Defence: Exchange tactic

explanations.explanation: With the queens facing on the open file, White can use Bxf7+ to force a favorable sequence of exchanges.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Ngf6 dxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 dxe5 Bxf7
explanation.title: Philidor Defence: Exchange tactic

explanations.explanation: The bishop check exploits the exposed queens: after ...Kxf7, Qxd8 wins the queen temporarily.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Ngf6 dxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 dxe5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qxd8
explanation.title: Philidor Defence: Exchange tactic

explanations.explanation: White has captured the queen on d8. Black can answer ...Bb4+ with a discovered attack and regain it, but must give back the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 d6 d4 Nd7 Bc4 Ngf6 dxe5 Nxe5 Nxe5 dxe5 Bxf7 Kxf7 Qxd8 Bb4
explanation.title: Philidor Defence: Exchange tactic

explanations.explanation: The bishop gives check and uncovers the rook's attack on White's queen. Qd2 interposes while attacking the bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 d4 exd4 c3 dxc3 Bc4 cxb2 Bxb2 d5
explanation.title: Danish Gambit: Schlechter Defence

explanations.explanation: Black returns material with ...d5, challenging the center and opening a line for the c8 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4 g4 O-O gxf3
explanation.title: King's Gambit: Muzio Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black accepts the knight sacrifice. White can recapture with Qxf3 and use the open f-file to attack.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 Bc4 g4 O-O gxf3 Qxf3 Qf6
explanation.title: King's Gambit: Muzio Gambit

explanations.explanation: The queen on f6 defends f7 and f4, while blocking White's pressure down the f-file.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 Nf6 Bc4 d5
explanation.title: King's Gambit: Kieseritzky Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's pawn attacks the bishop and also attacks e4; White can capture on d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 exf4 Nf3 g5 h4 g4 Ne5 d6
explanation.title: King's Gambit: Kieseritzky Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black attacks the knight on e5 with ...d6. White can capture the advanced g4 pawn with Nxg4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 f4 Bc5 fxe5 Qh4
explanation.title: King's Gambit Declined: Queen check

explanations.explanation: Black's queen gives check. White can block with g3; moving the king to e2 instead permits ...Qxe4 mate.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 Na6 Bxa6 Qa5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Unusual knight sacrifice

explanations.explanation: Black's queen gives check and attacks the bishop on a6. White can block with Nc3.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nd7 Ng5 h6 Ne6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Smothered Mate Variation

explanations.explanation: White's knight attacks the bishop, exploiting the weaknesses left by ...h6 and the open h5–e8 diagonal.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop to g6. White can continue Ne2 and Nf4 to attack it again.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: The knight attacks the bishop, threatening to damage Black's kingside pawns if it captures.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4 Bh7 Nxh5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: White wins the h5 pawn, but Black has counterplay against the d4 pawn on the other side of the board.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4 Bh7 Nxh5 Nc6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight against d4, adding pressure to the center after giving up the h-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O Nge7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Botvinnik-Carls Defence

explanations.explanation: Black's knight heads for f5. White can develop Be3 to reinforce d4 or choose another developing move.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 e6 Be3 Nh6 Bxh6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Botvinnik-Carls Defence

explanations.explanation: White has taken the knight on h6. After ...gxh6 Black gains the two bishops and an open g-file, at the cost of a damaged pawn structure.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 dxc5 e6 Be3 Nh6 c3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Botvinnik-Carls Defence

explanations.explanation: White supports d4 with the c-pawn, preparing a retreat square for the bishop. Black's knight can head to f5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Qc7 h3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 6. h3

explanations.explanation: The h-pawn controls g4, discouraging ...Bg4. Black must choose another way to develop the c8 bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bg5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: The bishop pins the f6 knight, increasing pressure on d5. Black can defend the pawn or capture on c4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bg5 dxc4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black captures on c4. Recapturing with the bishop can leave White with an isolated d-pawn and active development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Bg5 dxc4 Bxc4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White's bishop recaptures, accepting an isolated d-pawn in return for activity. Black may challenge the g5 bishop with ...h6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can choose the solid ...e6, a fianchetto with ...g6, or the active ...Bg4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black develops the bishop outside the pawn chain. White can exchange on d5 or continue development with Be3, Bg5 or Be2.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black's knight recaptures on d5. White can play Qb3, putting immediate pressure on Black's position.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White's queen attacks the d5 knight. Black can exchange on f3 and damage White's pawn structure.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black has taken the knight on f3. White normally recaptures with the g-pawn, accepting doubled pawns for active play.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White has doubled f-pawns but retains attacking chances. Black can defend the d5 knight with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black's e-pawn defends the knight. White can take on b7 and try to make the most of the active queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6 Qxb7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White has captured b7; Black can counterattack with ...Nxd4, taking advantage of White's compromised center.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6 Qxb7 Nxd4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black's knight takes on d4. White can keep the initiative with Bb5+, checking before deciding how to recover material.
