explanations.explanation: White's bishop pins the f6 knight, indirectly defending e4. Black can challenge the center with ...c5.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c5 cxd5 exd5
explanation.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Tarrasch Defence

explanations.explanation: Black's e-pawn recaptures on d5, preserving a central pawn. White can develop the knights and fianchetto the king's bishop.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 c4 e6 Nc3 c6 e4 dxe4 Nxe4 Bb4 Bd2
explanation.title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Marshall Gambit

explanations.explanation: White's bishop blocks the check and attacks its counterpart, but Black can take d4 with the queen.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Bc4
explanation.title: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: 3. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop toward f7, seeking rapid activity for the gambit pawn.

explanation.moves: d4 d5 e4 dxe4 Bc4 Nc6
explanation.title: Blackmar-Diemer Gambit: 3...Nc6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can bring the queen to h5 to increase pressure on f7.

explanation.moves: d4 d6 c4 e5 dxe5
explanation.title: Old Indian Defence: 3. dxe5

explanations.explanation: White captures on e5. Black can recapture with ...dxe5 or offer the Lisbon Gambit with ...Nc6.

explanation.moves: d4 d6 c4 e5 dxe5 Nc6
explanation.title: Old Indian Defence: Lisbon Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight instead of immediately recapturing on e5. Taking another pawn with exd6 calls for accuracy.

explanation.moves: d4 f5 Bg5 h6 Bh4
explanation.title: Dutch Defence: 2. Bg5

explanations.explanation: White retreats the bishop to h4. If Black advances ...g5, the bishop can drop to g3 and White can challenge the weakened kingside.

explanation.moves: d4 f5 h4 Nf6 h5 h6
explanation.title: Dutch Defence: Early h-pawn advance

explanations.explanation: Black plays ...h6, stopping the pawn on h5 but weakening light squares around the king, including g6.

explanation.moves: Nc3 b5
explanation.title: Van Geet Opening: Laroche Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's b-pawn gains queenside space and offers a pawn. After Nxb5, Black can build a center with ...c6 and ...d5.

explanation.moves: Nh3 d5
explanation.title: Amar Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies d5 and opens the c8 bishop's diagonal, introducing the possibility of ...Bxh3 and doubled h-pawns.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 1...e6

explanations.explanation: White's bishop pressures g7. Capturing the b4 pawn with the bishop can allow Bxg7.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 2...Nf6

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight instead of taking b4 and allowing the bishop to capture on g7.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 3. b5

explanations.explanation: White advances the b-pawn out of the bishop's path. Black can challenge it with ...a6 or establish the center with ...d5.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5 a6 a4 axb5
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 4...axb5

explanations.explanation: Black captures the b5 pawn. White can recapture with the a-pawn; the b2 bishop protects the rook on a1.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5 a6 a4 axb5 axb5
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 5. axb5

explanations.explanation: White's rook attacks the a8 rook on the opened file. Black can exchange rooks on a1.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5 a6 a4 axb5 axb5 Rxa1 Bxa1
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 6. Bxa1

explanations.explanation: White's bishop recaptures after the rook exchange. Both sides can now develop in several ways.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5 b6
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 3...b6

explanations.explanation: Black prepares to fianchetto the c8 bishop, contesting the long diagonal.

explanation.moves: b4 e6 Bb2 Nf6 b5 d5 e3
explanation.title: Polish Opening: 4. e3

explanations.explanation: White supports the center with e3 and opens a path for the f1 bishop.

explanation.moves: c3 d5
explanation.title: Saragossa Opening: 1...d5

explanations.explanation: Black's d-pawn controls e4 and c4. White can play d4 and enter a queen's pawn structure.

explanation.moves: c4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 g3 g6 Bg2 Bg7
explanation.title: English Opening: Symmetrical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black completes the kingside fianchetto. White can castle or develop the b1 knight to c3.

explanation.moves: f3 e5 c3
explanation.title: Barnes Opening: 2. c3

explanations.explanation: White's c-pawn supports d4, though it also occupies the b1 knight's natural square.

explanation.moves: f3 e5 g4
explanation.title: Barnes Opening: Fool's Mate

explanations.explanation: White's g-pawn advance opens the diagonal to the king. Black can deliver immediate mate with ...Qh4#.

explanation.moves: f4 d5 g4
explanation.title: Bird Opening: 2. g4

explanations.explanation: White advances the g-pawn, weakening the kingside and offering a pawn. Black can take it or strike the center with ...e5.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 Nc6
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight, a sideline to the more common ...d6. White should watch for checks along the h4–e1 diagonal.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 Nc6 Nf3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. This avoids the tactical problem of an immediate d4 followed by ...Qh4+.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 Nc6 Nf3 g5 d4 g4 Ng5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White retreats the knight to g5 after ...g4. Black can challenge it or strike the center.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 Nc6 d4 Qh4
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's queen gives check and also attacks d4. White must address both threats.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 Nc6 d4 Qh4 g3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White's g-pawn blocks the check and attacks the queen. Black can capture the d4 pawn next.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 Nf3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops Nf3 before resolving the d6 pawn, allowing a transposition into a more familiar From's Gambit line.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 Nf3 dxe5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures the pawn on e5. White can take with Nxe5 or instead build the center with e4.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 Nf3 dxe5 Nxe5
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White's knight captures on e5, accepting the gambit. Black can develop ...Bd6 with pressure on the kingside.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 exd6 Bxd6 Nf3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can advance ...g5, the aggressive Lasker Variation.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 exd6 Bxd6 Nf3 g5 g3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White's g-pawn strengthens the kingside and gives the f3 knight h4 as a possible retreat.

explanation.moves: f4 e5 fxe5 d6 exd6 Bxd6 h4 Bg3
explanation.title: Bird Opening: From's Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's bishop checkmates on the weakened diagonal after White's h-pawn advance.

explanation.moves: g3 h5
explanation.title: Hungarian Opening: 1...h5

explanations.explanation: Black advances the h-pawn, with the idea of continuing to h4 and opening the h-file.

explanation.moves: g3 h5 Nf3 h4 Nxh4 Rxh4
explanation.title: Hungarian Opening: Van Kuijk Gambit

explanations.explanation: Black's rook captures on h4, sacrificing an exchange to open lines on the kingside.

explanation.moves: h4 d5 h5
explanation.title: Kádas Opening: 2. h5

explanations.explanation: White advances the h-pawn again, while Black can occupy the center with ...e5.

explanation.moves: h4 d5 h5 e5
explanation.title: Kádas Opening: 2...e5

explanations.explanation: Black occupies e5 alongside the d5 pawn. White can continue h6 or prepare d4 with c3.

explanation.moves: h4 d5 h5 e5 h6
explanation.title: Kádas Opening: Croon's Gambit

explanations.explanation: White advances the h-pawn, offering it to open the rook file or establish an advanced pawn on the kingside.

explanation.moves: h4 d5 h5 h6
explanation.title: Kádas Opening: 2...h6

explanations.explanation: Black's h-pawn blocks White's h-pawn from advancing farther.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 Nc6 Bb5 a6
explanation.title: Sicilian Defence: Rossolimo Variation

explanations.explanation: Black's a-pawn attacks the bishop. White can carry out the planned exchange on c6.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 a6 h4
explanation.title: Sicilian Defence: Najdorf Variation

explanations.explanation: White advances the h-pawn, beginning an aggressive kingside plan against the Najdorf setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be2
explanation.title: Sicilian Defence: Classical Dragon

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, preparing to castle and build a solid kingside setup.

explanation.moves: e4 c5 Nf3 d6 d4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nf6 Nc3 g6 Be3 Ng4 Bb5
explanation.title: Sicilian Defence: Dragon Variation

explanations.explanation: White's bishop gives check, disrupting Black's coordination after ...Ng4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

explanations.explanation: White develops the second knight. Black can pin it with ...Bg4 or exchange on e4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

explanations.explanation: White's pawn attacks the knight. Black often centralizes it on e4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e5 Ne4 d4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

explanations.explanation: White advances d4, building a center. Black can capture the c3 knight and prompt a recapture.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 Nf6 e5 Ne4 d4 Nxc3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges the knight on c3. White can recapture with the b-pawn, shaping the queenside pawn structure.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 Nc3 d5 Nf3 dxe4 Nxe4 Nf6 Qe2 Nxe4 Qxe4 Nd7 d4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Two Knights Attack

explanations.explanation: White plays d4, establishing a center. Black can develop ...Nf6 with an attack on the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng3 Bg6 h4 h6 Nf3 Nd7 h5 Bh7 Bd3 Bxd3 Qxd3 e6 Bf4 Qa5 Bd2 Bb4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: Black's bishop attacks the d2 bishop. White can maintain more pieces with c3 or Ne4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: 5. Ng5

explanations.explanation: White moves the knight to g5, escaping the bishop's attack and pointing toward Black's kingside.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 Bg6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: 5. Ng5

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop to g6, preserving it after the white knight left e4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Bf5 Ng5 Bg6 N1f3 h6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: 5. Ng5

explanations.explanation: Black's h-pawn attacks the knight. White can retreat to h3 and aim for f4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nc3 dxe4 Nxe4 Qd5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: 4...Qd5

explanations.explanation: Black develops the queen with an attack on e4, choosing an unusual and sharp alternative to the usual bishop or knight development.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 Nd2 dxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Defence: 3. Nd2

explanations.explanation: Black captures on e4. Nxe4 recovers the pawn and can transpose into a main-line Caro-Kann position.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: White's g-pawn attacks the bishop, gaining kingside space. Black can retreat to g6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: Black strikes at d4 with the c-pawn. White can continue to harass the bishop with h4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 Bf5 Nc3 e6 g4 Bg6 Nge2 c5 h4 h5 Nf4 Bh7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Van der Wiel Attack

explanations.explanation: Black retreats the bishop to h7, allowing White's knight to take the h5 pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4 Be2
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Botvinnik-Carls Defence

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop and can castle. Black has time to continue development with ...e6.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 cxd4 cxd4 Bg4 Be2 e6 O-O
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Advance: Botvinnik-Carls Defence

explanations.explanation: White has castled with the king on g1. Black can pressure d4 with ...Qb6 or aim a knight at f5 with ...Ne7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 7. Qb3

explanations.explanation: White's queen attacks b7. Black can defend with ...Qc8 or ...Qd7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3 Qd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 7...Qd7

explanations.explanation: Black's queen defends b7 and leaves queenside castling available. White commonly develops Nd2.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 Bd3 Nc6 c3 Nf6 Bf4 Bg4 Qb3 Qd7 Nd2 e6 Ngf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann Exchange: 9. Ngf3

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight. Black can exchange the g4 bishop for it or postpone the decision.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White captures on d5. Black can recapture with the knight and keep the position active.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6 Qxb7 Nxd4 Bb5 Nxb5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black's knight captures the checking bishop. White can recapture immediately or insert Qc6+ first.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6 Qxb7 Nxd4 Bb5 Nxb5 Qc6
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: White's queen gives check before recovering the knight. Black must find a response that protects the rook on a8.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 exd5 cxd5 c4 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6 Nf3 Bg4 cxd5 Nxd5 Qb3 Bxf3 gxf3 e6 Qxb7 Nxd4 Bb5 Nxb5 Qc6 Ke7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Panov Attack

explanations.explanation: Black moves the king to e7. White can recapture on b5 or keep up the attack with Qc5+.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: White recaptures with the f-pawn on e4, building a broad center. Black can challenge it immediately with ...e5.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the knight with an attack on e5. Black can pin it with ...Bg4.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 Bg4 Bc4 Nd7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can castle or prepare Qb3 with c3 to increase pressure on f7 and b7.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 dxe4 fxe4 e5 Nf3 Bg4 Bc4 Nd7 O-O Ngf6 dxe5
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: White captures on e5. An immediate ...Nxe5 allows Qxd8, escaping the pin by exchanging queens.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: Black develops the knight. White can bring the queen to d3 or d2 and prepare queenside castling.

explanation.moves: e4 c6 d4 d5 f3 e6 Nc3 Bb4 Bf4 Ne7 Qd3
explanation.title: Caro-Kann: Fantasy Variation

explanations.explanation: White develops the queen. Black can try ...b6 and ...Ba6 to exchange the light-squared bishop.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Bc4
explanation.title: French Defence: 2. Bc4

explanations.explanation: White develops the bishop, but Black can strike the center and attack it with ...d5.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 Bc4 d5
explanation.title: French Defence: 2. Bc4

explanations.explanation: Black's d-pawn attacks the bishop while challenging White's center.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3
explanation.title: French Defence: Winawer Variation

explanations.explanation: Black exchanges on c3 with check rather than retreating the bishop. White can recapture with the b-pawn.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Bb4 e5 c5 a3 Bxc3 bxc3 Ne7 Qg4 Qc7 Qxg7
explanation.title: French Defence: Winawer Poisoned Pawn

explanations.explanation: White's queen takes g7 and attacks the rook. Black can respond ...Rg8, attacking the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 Nc3 Nf6 Bg5 Be7 e5 Nfd7 Bxe7
explanation.title: French Defence: Classical Variation

explanations.explanation: White exchanges on e7. Black can recapture with the queen, keeping the king safe.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4
explanation.title: French Defence: Advance Variation

explanations.explanation: White recaptures on d4. If ...Nxd4, Nxd4 Qxd4, Bb5+ discovers an attack on Black's queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: French Defence: Advance Variation

explanations.explanation: Black takes the d4 pawn, but White can take the knight and exploit the discovered-attack tactic if the queen recaptures.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nxd4
explanation.title: French Defence: Advance Variation

explanations.explanation: White's knight captures on d4. After ...Qxd4, Bb5+ discovers an attack on the queen.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 e5 c5 c3 Nc6 Nf3 Qb6 Bd3 cxd4 cxd4 Nxd4 Nxd4 Qxd4 Bb5
explanation.title: French Defence: Advance Variation

explanations.explanation: White's bishop checks and uncovers the d1 queen's attack on the black queen at d4.

explanation.moves: e4 e6 d4 d5 exd5
explanation.title: French Defence: Exchange Variation

explanations.explanation: White exchanges on d5, entering the Exchange Variation. Black can recapture with the e-pawn to retain a central presence.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Ng4 Bg5 f6
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: Black's f-pawn attacks the bishop and blocks its attack on the queen. White can capture the pawn with exf6.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Ng4 Bg5 f6 exf6 gxf6
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: Black recaptures on f6 with the g-pawn, attacking the bishop on g5. White can retreat Bh4.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Bc5 b4 Bxb4 c3 Ba5 d4 Nf6 dxe5 Nxe4
explanation.title: Evans Gambit: Knight Defence

explanations.explanation: Black takes the e4 pawn, but Qd5 attacks the knight and threatens mate on f7.

explanation.moves: e4 e5 Nf3 Nc6 Bc4 Nf6 Ng5 d5 exd5 Na5 Bb5 c6
explanation.title: Two Knights Defence: Main line

explanations.explanation: Black's c-pawn blocks the check and attacks the bishop on b5. White can capture the pawn with dxc6.
